=== site README ===
# deadreckon-site

Marketing site for [deadreckon](https://github.com/deadreckon/deadreckon), the
harness around the agent CLI you already use.

Built with Astro. Static output. One page so far; the page is the product
brief, the docs live in the deadreckon repo.

## Run it

```bash
bun install
bun run dev      # local dev server on http://localhost:4321
bun run build    # static output to ./dist
```

Use `pnpm` or `npm` if you prefer; the lockfile is bun's.

## Editorial rules

Copy follows the rules in `/Users/gdc/impeccable/STYLE.md` (no em dashes, no
"delve", no "seamless", no "let's dive in"). When you edit the page, read that
file first.

Two cardinal rules specific to this site:

1. **Don't oversell the watchdog.** The `dr-gate` signature is a hash plus
   filesystem isolation of the nonce, not crypto. Say so on the page and in
   the FAQ. The integrity story is real; the precise framing is what makes it
   trustworthy.
2. **Mention real commands, not hypothetical ones.** Every command in a code
   block should be one you can paste into a working deadreckon install.

## Structure

```
src/
  layouts/Base.astro    one shared layout (header + footer)
  components/
    Header.astro        sticky top nav
    Footer.astro
  pages/
    index.astro         the whole homepage
  styles/
    tokens.css          colors, type, spacing, motion
    main.css            page-section styles
public/
  assets/               wordmark, icon, logo (copied from deadreckon repo)
```

## Brand

- **Wordmark green** is the accent. Pulled from the deadreckon wordmark
  (`docs/assets/deadreckon-wordmark.png` in the deadreckon repo).
- **Bone paper** is the background. Warm, low-contrast, easy on long reads.
- **JetBrains Mono** carries headings. The product is a CLI; the type should
  say so.
- **Inter** is the body. Workhorse.

If you change accent colors, change them in `tokens.css` (`--signal`,
`--signal-deep`, `--signal-ink`, `--signal-wash`) and audit the terminal
palette below; the green is shared between brand and terminal output.
```

=== impeccable README (head) ===
# Impeccable

The vocabulary you didn't know you needed. 1 skill, 23 commands, and curated anti-patterns for impeccable frontend design.

> **Quick start:** Visit [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style) to download ready-to-use bundles.

## Why Impeccable?

Anthropic's [frontend-design](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/main/skills/frontend-design) was the first widely-used design skill for Claude. Impeccable started from there.

Every model trained on the same SaaS templates. Skip the guidance and you get the same handful of tells on every project: Inter for everything, purple-to-blue gradients, cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, the rounded-square icon tile above every heading.

Impeccable adds:
- **7 domain reference files** ([view source](skill/)). Typography, color, motion, spatial, interaction, responsive, UX writing. Load on every command, alongside a brand-vs-product register that adjusts the defaults.
- **23 commands.** A shared design vocabulary with your AI: `polish`, `audit`, `critique`, `distill`, `animate`, `bolder`, `quieter`, and more.
- **27 deterministic anti-pattern rules** plus a 12-rule LLM critique pass. CLI and browser extension run the deterministic ones with no LLM and no API key. Each is tied to specific design guidance the skill teaches against.

## What's Included

### The Skill: impeccable

A comprehensive design skill with 7 domain-specific references ([view skill](skill/SKILL.src.md)):

| Reference | Covers |
|-----------|--------|
| [typography](skill/reference/typography.md) | Type systems, font pairing, modular scales, OpenType |
| [color-and-contrast](skill/reference/color-and-contrast.md) | OKLCH, tinted neutrals, dark mode, accessibility |
| [spatial-design](skill/reference/spatial-design.md) | Spacing systems, grids, visual hierarchy |
| [motion-design](skill/reference/motion-design.md) | Easing curves, staggering, reduced motion |
| [interaction-design](skill/reference/interaction-design.md) | Forms, focus states, loading patterns |
| [responsive-design](skill/reference/responsive-design.md) | Mobile-first, fluid design, container queries |
| [ux-writing](skill/reference/ux-writing.md) | Button labels, error messages, empty states |

### 23 Commands

All commands are accessed through `/impeccable`:

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `/impeccable craft` | Full shape-then-build flow with visual iteration |

=== release/install.sh head ===
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

repo="${DEADRECKON_REPO:-gregce/deadreckon}"
tag="${DEADRECKON_TAG:-v0.1.0-rc.1}"
asset="${DEADRECKON_INSTALLER_ASSET:-deadreckon-installer.sh}"
base_url="https://github.com/${repo}/releases/download/${tag}"
tmp="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/deadreckon-install.$$"

die() {
  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

download() {
  url="$1"
  out="$2"
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$out"
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wget -qO "$out" "$url"
  else
    die "install curl or wget, then rerun this installer"
  fi
}

cleanup() {
  rm -rf "$tmp"
}

trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM

(umask 077 && mkdir "$tmp") || die "could not create temp dir: $tmp"

printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: ${repo} ${tag}"
download "${base_url}/${asset}" "${tmp}/${asset}" || die "could not download ${base_url}/${asset}"

if download "${base_url}/SHA256SUMS" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS"; then
  if grep "  ${asset}\$" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS" > "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS.${asset}"; then
    if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      (cd "$tmp" && shasum -a 256 -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
    elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      (cd "$tmp" && sha256sum -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
    else
      printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: shasum/sha256sum not found; skipping checksum verification" >&2
    fi
  else
    printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: ${asset} was not listed in SHA256SUMS" >&2

# STYLE.md

Editorial brief for impeccable.design. Read this before writing or editing user-facing copy: the homepage, sub-pages, command editorials, tutorials, and READMEs.

The bar: **for every paragraph, point to the sentence that makes it specifically yours.** If you can't, the paragraph is AI by default, even if a human typed it.

## Principles

1. **Open with the reader's wrong belief, your strongest claim, or the example.** No "in this guide", no "let's dive in".
2. **Take a position someone could disagree with.** If the paragraph could be inverted without changing meaning, it has no position. Sign your stance.
3. **Name names. Use numbers.** Real competitors, real customer names, real version numbers, real file paths, real benchmarks. Cut "lightweight"; write "54 KB".
4. **Verbs lead. Nouns follow.** Imperative is fine. Active voice. Cut nominalizations ("the implementation of" → "implementing").
5. **Vary sentence length on purpose.** Long, long, short. Smooth uniform rhythm is the deepest AI tell.
6. **Prose carries the load; structure supports it.** Bullets are for parallel options. Paragraphs are for argument. Don't bullet what would be tighter as a sentence.
7. **Plain words. Technical terms only when something specifically rests on them.** Mixing levels lets the technical terms hit harder.
8. **Allow ungrammatical fragments for rhythm.** Five words. Confidence signal.
9. **Respect the reader's competence.** No "developers should consider"; just "you might not need an effect".
10. **Read it aloud. Fix anything you stumble over.**
11. **Concrete over comprehensive.** Coverage is an AI obsession. Trade coverage for momentum. Leave things out.
12. **Close by handing off the next move.** Don't summarize. End on the strongest sentence, give a directive ("Now do this"), or just stop.

## Denylist

The build's `validateProse` step (in `scripts/build.js`) fails the build on these. The list is the editorial brief, enforced. Add a rule here when you ban a new pattern; remove a rule when the term has earned a real meaning here. **Do not silently allowlist** by working around the regex.

### Stolen-engineer diction
Engineering words that became AI flavor once they leaked into training data around late 2024.

| Banned | Why | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `load-bearing` | Almost always vague. The literal sense is rare. | Name the specific thing it does. "The decision that shapes the rest", "carries the brand", "matters specifically". |
| `highest-leverage` | Vague claim of impact. | Say what specifically pays off. "The change that moves the design most". |
| `biggest unlock` | Marketing-speak. | Describe the actual change. |

### Internal jargon leaking out
Words that work in a research notebook and fail in user copy.

| Banned | Why | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `reflex defaults` | Eval-team jargon. | "Instincts", "first guesses", "default reaches". |
| `collapses into monoculture` | Eval-paper voice. | Describe what specifically went wrong (e.g. "every model picked the same three fonts"). |
| `data-driven` | Empty marketing adjective. | Cite the data. "Validated against 15 briefs across two models". |

### Marketing voice
Adjectives and verbs that gesture at quality without doing the work.

| Banned | Why | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `seamless`, `seamlessly` | Hollow positive. | Say what specifically works without friction. |
| `robust`, `robustness` | Hollow positive. | Cite the failure mode handled. |
| `elevate`, `elevates` | Marketing verb. | Use the specific verb (improve, raise, sharpen). |
| `empower`, `empowers` | Marketing verb. | "Let you", "make possible". |
| `underscore`, `underscores` | AI tell. | "Show", "make clear". |
| `pivotal` | Hollow positive. | "Central", "key", or describe the role. |
| `tapestry` | AI scenery noun. | Cut. |

### Verbs
| Banned | Why | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `delve`, `delves`, `delved`, `delving` | The most-flagged AI tell of all. | "Look at", "explore", or just delete the throat-clearing verb. |

```text
1	<p align="center">
2	  <img src="docs/assets/deadreckon-wordmark.png" alt="deadreckon logo" width="640">
3	</p>
4	
5	<p align="center"><strong>Run your coding agent unattended, and trust the result.</strong></p>
6	
7	<p align="center">
8	DeadReckon is a harness around the agent CLI you already use.<br>
9	A separate watchdog process, not the agent, decides when the work is actually done.<br>
10	You get a signed, auditable artifact instead of a chat transcript you have to take on faith.
11	</p>
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Get started
16	
17	```bash
18	cargo build --release          # binary at ./target/release/deadreckon
19	```
20	
21	Then the whole tool is five commands:
22	
23	| Command | What it does |
24	|---|---|
25	| `deadreckon start "build the app"` | Kick off a supervised run. Walk away. |
26	| `deadreckon attach latest` | Watch it work live. `Ctrl-D` leaves it running. |
27	| `deadreckon status` | What happened, and the one thing to do next. |
28	| `deadreckon list` | Find recent runs and plans. |
29	| `deadreckon finish latest` | Apply it to your branch, or export it. |
30	
31	For a higher-level read while it runs, `deadreckon attach latest --view narrative` shows cited prose plus an evidence-backed visual map.
32	
33	<p align="center">
34	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/claude-logo.png" alt="Claude Code" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
35	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/openai-logo.png" alt="Codex" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
36	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/gemini-logo.png" alt="Gemini CLI" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
37	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/github-logo.png" alt="GitHub Copilot CLI" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
38	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/opencode-logo.png" alt="OpenCode" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
39	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/pi-logo.svg" alt="Pi" height="34">
40	</p>
41	
42	<p align="center"><sub>Supervises the agent CLI you already use: Claude Code · Codex · Gemini · Copilot · OpenCode · Pi · or any Anthropic / OpenAI-compatible API.</sub></p>
43	
44	Everything else (budgets, undo, multi-step chains, provider routing) is optional power you reach for later. No API keys? `deadreckon run "hello" --smoke --sandbox none` exercises the whole harness against a faked provider.
45	
46	> [!TIP]
47	> DeadReckon is on the production-release track. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, orchestration, and apply) is implemented and tested; release notes call out any compatibility migrations.
48	
49	## Why it's different
50	
51	- **It can't fake the finish.** A separate watchdog (`dr-gate`) holds a secret the agent process can't read and signs the result with it. No valid signature, no "done." The agent literally cannot mark its own work accepted.
52	- **Walk away for real.** Every turn is saved to disk. Close your laptop, lose the network, kill the model, then attach from another terminal and resume from the last completed turn.
53	- **Evidence, not a transcript.** Each accepted run promotes to a reviewable artifact: what changed, why, which prompt touched which file, what it spent.
54	
55	→ The full story (the loop, the mental model, and how it compares) is in **[Concepts & How It Works](docs/CONCEPTS.md)**.
56	
57	## Documentation
58	
59	| Doc | What's inside |
60	|---|---|
61	| **[Concepts & How It Works](docs/CONCEPTS.md)** | The loop, the watchdog, the mental model, supported agents, how it compares |
62	| **[HOWTO](HOWTO.md)** | Practical usage: setup, providers, sandboxes, configuration, every command |
63	| **[DESIGN](DESIGN.md)** | Product and architecture intent |
64	| **[As-Built Architecture](docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | Detailed implementation reference |
65	| **[Resume Semantics](docs/RESUME-SEMANTICS.md)** · **[Multi-Run](docs/MULTI-RUN.md)** | Crash/resume behavior and concurrency rules |
66	| **[V1 Candidates](docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md)** | Deferred features and roadmap |
67	
68	DeadReckon is maintained as production-release software. The core lifecycle is implemented and tested, alongside multi-agent orchestration (`plan` / `fork` / `merge`), autonomous chains, the provider flight recorder with `rewind`, and a local self-improvement loop (`learn` / `improve`).
69

94	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">The mechanic</span>
95	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">A separate process decides when the run is done. <em>The agent is not in the room.</em></h2>
96	      <p class="section-lead reveal">
97	        Every unattended-agent product runs into the same problem: the agent decides when it's
98	        finished. The transcript looks confident. The tests aren't run. You shipped a lie.
99	        deadreckon fixes this with a 33-line companion binary, <code>dr-gate</code>, that runs
100	        outside the agent's sandbox and signs the result. The marker is what unlocks promotion.
101	      </p>
102	
103	      <div class="quickstart">
104	        <div class="term reveal" aria-label="The dr-gate watchdog rejecting a forged marker">
105	          <div class="term-bar">
106	            <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
107	            <span class="term-title">dr-gate · watchdog</span>
108	          </div>
109	          <pre class="term-body">
110	<span class="meta"># inside the run's sandbox</span>
111	<span class="prompt">agent$</span> <span class="you">cat /run/gate/nonce</span>
112	<span class="fail">cat: /run/gate/nonce: Permission denied</span>
113	
114	<span class="prompt">agent$</span> <span class="you">echo '&#123;"ok":true&#125;'</span> &gt; proofs/turn-acceptance.json
115	<span class="prompt">agent$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon finish latest</span>
116	<span class="fail">refused: marker signature missing</span>
117	<span class="fail">       expected: nonce-derived hash, got: empty</span>
118	
119	<span class="meta"># meanwhile, outside the sandbox</span>
120	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">dr-gate sign</span>
121	<span class="out">  read    </span>$RUN/gate/nonce <span class="ok">(0600, root-owned for this run)</span>
122	<span class="out">  hashed  </span>nonce + marker fields
123	<span class="out">  wrote   </span>proofs/turn-acceptance.json
124	<span class="ok">  signed ✓</span>
125	          </pre>
126	        </div>
127	
128	        <div class="quickstart-steps reveal">
129	          <div class="qs-step">
130	            <strong>01 · Isolated nonce</strong>
131	            <p>
132	              At run start, deadreckon writes a UUID nonce to <code>gate/nonce</code> outside the
133	              agent's sandbox root. The agent process has no read path to it.
134	            </p>
135	          </div>
136	          <div class="qs-step">
137	            <strong>02 · Out-of-band signature</strong>
138	            <p>
139	              <code>dr-gate</code> is a separate binary. It reads the nonce, hashes it with the
140	              acceptance fields, and writes the marker to <code>proofs/turn-acceptance.json</code>.
141	            </p>
142	          </div>
143	          <div class="qs-step">
144	            <strong>03 · Refusal by default</strong>
145	            <p>
146	              The main binary verifies the marker against the nonce before promotion. No valid
147	              signature, no promotion. The run loops, the agent gets another turn.
148	            </p>
149	          </div>
150	          <div class="qs-step">
151	            <strong>Honest scope</strong>
152	            <p>
153	              The signature is a hash, not an HMAC. The security property is process isolation
154	              under the default sandbox (<code>sandbox-exec</code> on macOS,
155	              <code>bwrap</code> on Linux), not cryptography. Turn the sandbox off, you lose the
156	              guarantee.
157	            </p>
158	          </div>

232	          <h3 class="cap-title">Your checkout is never touched.</h3>
233	          <p>
234	            In a git repo, <code>deadreckon run</code> opens a separate worktree on a
235	            <code>dr/...</code> branch under <code>~/.deadreckon/worktrees/</code>. The agent
236	            writes there. Your checkout sits exactly where you left it until you choose to merge:

240	            <code>export</code> the finished tree to a new directory and never touch your branch
241	            at all. Worktrees, snapshots, and the launch directory are recorded so resumes find
242	            their way back even after a crash.
243	          </p>
244	          <div class="cap-meta">Modes: <b>worktree (default)</b> · copy · fresh · in-place</div>
245	        </div>
246	        <div class="cap-visual">
247	          <div class="term">
248	            <div class="term-bar">
249	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
250	              <span class="term-title">filesystem after `deadreckon run`</span>
251	            </div>
252	            <pre class="term-body">
253	<span class="out">~/code/myapp/                </span><span class="ok">← your checkout, unchanged</span>
254	<span class="out">  src/...</span>
255	<span class="out">  .git/</span>
256	
257	<span class="out">~/.deadreckon/worktrees/</span>
258	<span class="out">  myapp-m7q3-build-a1f2/      </span><span class="accent">← agent works here</span>
259	<span class="out">    src/...                   </span>(branch: dr/build-the-app)
260	<span class="out">    state.json</span>
261	<span class="out">    events.jsonl</span>
262	<span class="out">    spend.jsonl</span>
263	<span class="out">    snapshots/turn-1/ ... turn-N/</span>
264	<span class="out">    proofs/turn-acceptance.json</span>
265	
266	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">git -C ~/code/myapp status</span>
267	<span class="ok">nothing to commit, working tree clean</span>
268	            </pre>
269	          </div>
270	        </div>
271	      </div>
272	
273	      <div class="cap cap--flip reveal">
274	        <div class="cap-body">
275	          <span class="cap-num">02</span>
276	          <h3 class="cap-title">Close the terminal. Open another. Attach.</h3>
277	          <p>
278	            The run lives on disk, not in your terminal session. Every turn writes
279	            <code>state.json</code>, <code>events.jsonl</code>, <code>traces.jsonl</code>,
280	            <code>spend.jsonl</code>, and a working-directory snapshot under
281	            <code>~/.deadreckon/</code>. The run keeps going whether you're watching or not.
282	          </p>
283	          <p>
284	            Type <code>deadreckon attach latest</code> and the TUI replays where the run is,
285	            what it edited, what it spent, and how many acceptance checks have passed.
286	            <code>Ctrl-D</code> detaches without killing. <code>deadreckon kill</code> stops it
287	            cleanly. <code>resume</code> picks up from the last completed turn.
288	          </p>
289	          <div class="cap-meta">Polling cadence: <b>events.jsonl every 500ms</b> · same-process bus when local</div>
290	        </div>
291	        <div class="cap-visual">
292	          <div class="term">
293	            <div class="term-bar">
294	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
295	              <span class="term-title">deadreckon attach latest</span>
296	            </div>
297	            <pre class="term-body">
298	<span class="out">┌─ run m7q3 · build the app ─────────────┐</span>
299	<span class="out">│ turn 14   wall 1h:42m   spend  $4.18   │</span>
300	<span class="out">│ provider  cli:codex     ctx 38% / 200k │</span>
301	<span class="out">├─ acceptance ───────────────────────────┤</span>
302	<span class="out">│ </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰</span><span class="out"> cargo_test      passed           │</span>
303	<span class="out">│ </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰</span><span class="out"> file_exists     passed           │</span>
304	<span class="out">│ </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰</span><span class="out"> content_match   passed           │</span>
305	<span class="out">│ </span><span class="warn">▰▰▰▱▱</span><span class="out"> build_success   running...       │</span>
306	<span class="out">├─ activity ─────────────────────────────┤</span>
307	<span class="out">│ 14:32  edit  src/auth/session.rs       │</span>
308	<span class="out">│ 14:33  edit  src/auth/mod.rs           │</span>
309	<span class="out">│ 14:33  run   cargo test --lib auth     │</span>
310	<span class="out">│ 14:35        </span><span class="accent">dr-gate signing marker...</span><span class="out"> │</span>
311	<span class="out">└────────────────────────────────────────┘</span>
312	<span class="meta">Ctrl-D detach · Ctrl-C never (use `deadreckon kill`)</span>
313	            </pre>
314	          </div>
315	        </div>
316	      </div>
317	
318	      <div class="cap reveal">
319	        <div class="cap-body">
320	          <span class="cap-num">03</span>
321	          <h3 class="cap-title">Undo turn 7. Keep turns 1 through 6.</h3>
322	          <p>
323	            Snapshots happen at turn boundaries, on disk, independent of git. So you can rewind
324	            a single bad turn without rolling back the whole run or rewriting branch history.
325	            The undo lands in <code>traces.jsonl</code>; the rest of the run keeps going.
326	          </p>
327	          <p>
328	            This is not <code>git reset</code> with extra steps. It works on the run's own snapshot
329	            trail, which means it works on <code>--in-place</code> runs in dirty repos and on
330	            non-git working directories too.
331	          </p>
332	        </div>
333	        <div class="cap-visual">
334	          <div class="term">
335	            <div class="term-bar">
336	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
337	              <span class="term-title">deadreckon undo --turn 7</span>
338	            </div>
339	            <pre class="term-body">
340	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon undo --run m7q3 --turn 7</span>
341	<span class="out">  restoring  </span>snapshots/turn-6/ <span class="ok">(working dir)</span>
342	<span class="out">  trace      </span>logged: undo-from=7 to=6
343	<span class="out">  state      </span>head turn now 6 · history preserved
344	<span class="ok">  done.</span> resume with: deadreckon resume m7q3
345	
346	<span class="meta"># turns 1-6 still in history, snapshots still on disk</span>
347	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">ls snapshots/</span>
348	<span class="out">turn-1  turn-2  turn-3  turn-4  turn-5  turn-6  turn-7</span>
349	            </pre>
350	          </div>
351	        </div>
352	      </div>
353	
354	      <div class="cap cap--flip reveal">
355	        <div class="cap-body">
356	          <span class="cap-num">04</span>
357	          <h3 class="cap-title">Get a reviewable artifact, not just a chat log.</h3>
358	          <p>
359	            deadreckon records which model call touched which files in
360	            <code>provenance.jsonl</code>. When the gate signs off, it writes a narrative,
361	            a decisions log, and a file-lineage manifest. You read the artifact. You don't
362	            scroll a transcript.
363	          </p>
364	          <p>
365	            <code>deadreckon doc &lt;run-id&gt; --kind delta</code> proposes architecture-doc
366	            updates when the run was broad enough to need them. That's how you keep
367	            <code>AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md</code> honest.
368	          </p>
369	          <div class="cap-meta">Outputs: <b>RUN-NARRATIVE</b> · RUN-DECISIONS · RUN-AS-BUILT · AS-BUILT-DELTA · manifest.json</div>
370	        </div>
371	        <div class="cap-visual">
372	          <div class="term">
373	            <div class="term-bar">
374	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
375	              <span class="term-title">RUN-NARRATIVE.md (excerpt)</span>
376	            </div>
377	            <pre class="term-body">
378	<span class="out">## What changed</span>
379	
380	<span class="out">Added password-based signup, login, and a saved-drawing</span>
381	<span class="out">route. New routes live in </span><span class="accent">src/auth/</span><span class="out"> and </span><span class="accent">src/drawings/</span><span class="out">.</span>
382	
383	<span class="out">## Why</span>
384	
385	<span class="out">The acceptance spec asked for three flows. Turn 4</span>
386	<span class="out">discovered an existing `User` model in `src/db/users.rs`</span>
387	<span class="out">and reused it instead of adding a parallel table.</span>
388	
389	<span class="out">## Files touched (provenance.jsonl summary)</span>
390	
391	<span class="out">  src/auth/session.rs       turns 3, 5, 7, 9</span>
392	<span class="out">  src/auth/mod.rs           turns 3, 9</span>
393	<span class="out">  src/drawings/save.rs      turns 11, 12</span>
394	<span class="out">  migrations/0004_auth.sql  turn 3</span>
395	<span class="out">  tests/auth_test.rs        turns 6, 8, 10</span>
396	            </pre>
397	          </div>
398	        </div>
399	      </div>
400	
401	      <div class="cap reveal">
402	        <div class="cap-body">
403	          <span class="cap-num">05</span>
404	          <h3 class="cap-title">Cap the spend. Cap the wall clock. Walk away.</h3>
405	          <p>
406	            Every provider response appends a record to <code>spend.jsonl</code> and updates the
407	            run total. Direct API routes (Anthropic, OpenAI) track dollar cost.
408	            Subscription CLI routes cap by wall-clock time, since the subscription already
409	            paid the bill.
410	          </p>
411	          <p>
412	            Pass <code>--max-spend 15</code> or <code>--max-wall-seconds 1800</code> and the run
413	            stops itself at the cap. Cross a high-spend threshold without the flag and you get
414	            an explicit confirmation, so a script doesn't accidentally launch a $200 run.
415	          </p>
416	        </div>
417	        <div class="cap-visual">
418	          <div class="term">
419	            <div class="term-bar">
420	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
421	              <span class="term-title">deadreckon run --max-spend 15</span>
422	            </div>
423	            <pre class="term-body">
424	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-spend 15</span>
425	<span class="out">  spend cap     </span>$15.00
426	<span class="out">  wall cap      </span>none
427	<span class="out">  current spend </span>$0.00
428	<span class="out">  starting...</span>
429	
430	<span class="meta">...later...</span>
431	<span class="out">  turn 22 · spend $14.82 / $15.00</span>
432	<span class="warn">  cap reached after turn 22</span>
433	<span class="ok">  run paused cleanly · resume with: deadreckon resume latest</span>
434	            </pre>
435	          </div>
436	        </div>
437	      </div>
438	    </div>
439	  </section>
440	
441	  {/* ============================================ COMPARE ============================================ */}
442	  <section class="section" id="compare">
443	    <div class="wrap">
444	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Compared</span>
445	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">deadreckon doesn't replace your agent CLI. <em>It supervises it.</em></h2>
446	      <p class="section-lead reveal">
447	        Use the agent CLI you already trust for the coding. Use deadreckon for what the agent
448	        CLI was never designed to do: isolation, evidence, recovery, and a "done" you can
449	        defend.
450	      </p>
451	
452	      <table class="compare reveal" aria-label="Comparison with running the agent CLI directly">
453	        <thead>
454	          <tr>
455	            <th>Operational concern</th>
456	            <th>Agent CLI alone</th>
457	            <th>deadreckon supervising the CLI</th>
458	          </tr>
459	        </thead>
460	        <tbody>
461	          <tr>
462	            <td>Workspace safety</td>
463	            <td class="bare">Runs where you start it</td>
464	            <td class="dr">Isolated worktree by default. <b>Your checkout sits untouched until you say apply.</b></td>
465	          </tr>
466	          <tr>
467	            <td>Long-running attach</td>
468	            <td class="bare">Tied to the current terminal</td>
469	            <td class="dr">Run state is durable. <b>Attach from another terminal, or after a reboot.</b></td>
470	          </tr>
471	          <tr>
472	            <td>Spend control</td>
473	            <td class="bare">Visibility varies by provider</td>
474	            <td class="dr"><b>spend.jsonl per turn.</b> Hard caps on dollars or wall-clock.</td>
475	          </tr>
476	          <tr>
477	            <td>Undo</td>
478	            <td class="bare">Manual git, if it works</td>
479	            <td class="dr"><b>Snapshots every turn.</b> Restore turn 7 without losing 1–6.</td>
480	          </tr>
481	          <tr>
482	            <td>Provenance</td>
483	            <td class="bare">Transcript doesn't map cleanly to files</td>
484	            <td class="dr">Model/tool/file linkage written to <b>provenance.jsonl</b>.</td>
485	          </tr>
486	          <tr>
487	            <td>"Done" criteria</td>
488	            <td class="bare">The agent declares itself done</td>
489	            <td class="dr"><b>Out-of-process watchdog signs.</b> No marker, no promotion.</td>
490	          </tr>
491	          <tr>
492	            <td>Applying the work</td>
493	            <td class="bare">Tool-specific patch flow</td>
494	            <td class="dr"><b>apply · discard · export · extend</b> as first-class verbs.</td>
495	          </tr>
496	          <tr>
497	            <td>Multi-run coordination</td>
498	            <td class="bare">Left to the operator</td>
499	            <td class="dr">Scope/task locks prevent conflicting same-task runs.</td>
500	          </tr>
501	        </tbody>
502	      </table>
503	    </div>
504	  </section>
505

606	  <section class="section" id="install">
607	    <div class="wrap">
608	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Install</span>
609	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Install the RC. Prove the harness. Then choose your provider.</h2>
610	
611	      <div class="quickstart reveal">
612	        <div class="term">
613	          <div class="term-bar">
614	            <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
615	            <span class="term-title">install · configure · run</span>
616	          </div>
617	          <pre class="term-body">
618	<span class="meta"># install the current RC from GitHub Release assets</span>
619	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">curl -fsSL https://deadreckon.sh/install.sh | sh</span>
620	
621	<span class="meta"># prove the harness without provider keys</span>
622	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon try</span>
623	
624	<span class="meta"># check local setup and available providers</span>
625	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon doctor</span>
626	
627	<span class="meta"># go</span>
628	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon start "make a small safe change"</span>
629	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon attach latest</span>
630	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon finish latest</span>
631	          </pre>
632	        </div>
633	
634	        <div class="quickstart-steps">
635	          <div class="qs-step">
636	            <strong>Requirements</strong>
637	            <p>macOS or Linux, plus <code>curl</code> or <code>wget</code>. The RC installer downloads signed GitHub Release assets; no Rust toolchain is required.</p>
638	          </div>
639	          <div class="qs-step">
640	            <strong>Pin a version</strong>
641	            <p>The site installer defaults to <code>v0.1.0-rc.1</code>. Override by piping it into <code>DEADRECKON_TAG=v0.1.0-rc.1 sh</code>.</p>
642	          </div>
643	          <div class="qs-step">
644	            <strong>State on disk</strong>
645	            <p>Everything writes under <code>~/.deadreckon/</code>. Set <code>DEADRECKON_HOME</code> for sandbox-isolated tests.</p>
646	          </div>
647	          <div class="qs-step">
648	            <strong>Verify it works</strong>
649	            <p><code>deadreckon try</code> runs a keyless signed proof. <code>deadreckon doctor</code> checks config, providers, sandbox backends, disk, and runtime.</p>
650	          </div>
651	        </div>
652	      </div>
653	    </div>
654	  </section>

656	  {/* ============================================ NAME ============================================ */}
657	  <section class="section" id="name">
658	    <div class="wrap">
659	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">The name</span>
660	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Dead reckoning. <em>Navigation without perfect visibility.</em></h2>
661	      <p class="section-lead reveal">
662	        Sailors plotted dead reckoning when the stars were out of view. Track every move so you
663	        know where you are now. Long unattended agent runs face the same problem: partial context,
664	        a terminal that may be gone when you look back, a model that may have lied at turn 7.
665	        Don't trust the final answer. Navigate by evidence.
666	      </p>
667	      <p class="section-lead reveal">
668	        The questions deadreckon exists to answer:
669	      </p>
670	      <ul class="reveal" style="list-style:none; padding:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:var(--s-3); font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--fs-sm); color: var(--ink-soft);">
671	        <li>→ Where did the agent run, and what did it spend?</li>
672	        <li>→ Can I attach after closing the terminal?</li>
673	        <li>→ Can I undo turn 7 without rolling back the whole project?</li>
674	        <li>→ Can I prove the agent didn't mark its own work as accepted?</li>
675	      </ul>
676	    </div>
677	  </section>
678	
679	  {/* ============================================ FAQ ============================================ */}
680	  <section class="section" id="faq">
681	    <div class="wrap">
682	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">FAQ</span>
683	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Honest answers, including the ones that make this look smaller.</h2>
684	
685	      <div class="faq-list reveal">
686	        <div class="faq-item">
687	          <h3 class="faq-q">Does deadreckon replace Claude Code or Codex?</h3>
688	          <p class="faq-a">No. You still install the CLI you already use. deadreckon shells out to it, runs it inside an isolated worktree under a sandbox, and supervises the loop around it. The agent does the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.</p>
689	        </div>
690	
691	        <div class="faq-item">
692	          <h3 class="faq-q">Is the gate signature cryptographic?</h3>
693	          <p class="faq-a">No. The signature is a hash of the run nonce with the marker fields, written by a separate binary (<code>dr-gate</code>). The security property is filesystem isolation of <code>gate/nonce</code> under the default sandbox, not an HMAC or signing key. Run with <code>--sandbox none</code> and you lose the guarantee. The architecture docs spell out the scope.</p>
694	        </div>
695	
696	        <div class="faq-item">
697	          <h3 class="faq-q">What happens if the run crashes mid-turn?</h3>
698	          <p class="faq-a">The next <code>deadreckon resume</code> reads <code>events.jsonl</code> and <code>traces.jsonl</code>, ignores incomplete trailing entries, and restarts from the last completed turn. Snapshots are written at turn boundaries, so worst case you re-do one turn.</p>
699	        </div>
700	
701	        <div class="faq-item">
702	          <h3 class="faq-q">Can I run more than one at a time?</h3>
703	          <p class="faq-a">Yes. Each run scopes to a project; scope and task locks prevent two runs from clobbering the same workspace. <code>deadreckon list</code> shows everything in the current project, <code>--all</code> shows everything everywhere.</p>
704	        </div>
705	
706	        <div class="faq-item">
707	          <h3 class="faq-q">Does it work without a git repo?</h3>
708	          <p class="faq-a">Yes. Outside git, deadreckon falls back to copy mode (or <code>--in-place</code> if you insist). Worktrees are the default only when there's something to branch from.</p>
709	        </div>
710	
711	        <div class="faq-item">
712	          <h3 class="faq-q">What's still rough?</h3>
713	          <p class="faq-a">deadreckon is alpha. <code>deadreckon import</code> from other tools' histories lists what's there, but doesn't normalize it. Chains work but are deliberately tucked behind a separate subcommand. The Windows path isn't there yet; macOS and Linux are.</p>
714	        </div>
715	
716	        <div class="faq-item">
717	          <h3 class="faq-q">Where does state live?</h3>
718	          <p class="faq-a">Under <code>~/.deadreckon/</code> by default. Per-run: <code>state.json</code>, <code>events.jsonl</code>, <code>traces.jsonl</code>, <code>spend.jsonl</code>, <code>provenance.jsonl</code>, <code>snapshots/turn-N/</code>, <code>proofs/turn-acceptance.json</code>. Accepted runs are promoted to <code>~/.deadreckon/library/&lt;scope&gt;/&lt;run-id&gt;/</code>.</p>

```text
1	# STYLE.md
2	
3	Editorial brief for impeccable.design. Read this before writing or editing user-facing copy: the homepage, sub-pages, command editorials, tutorials, and READMEs.
4	
5	The bar: **for every paragraph, point to the sentence that makes it specifically yours.** If you can't, the paragraph is AI by default, even if a human typed it.
6	
7	## Principles
8	
9	1. **Open with the reader's wrong belief, your strongest claim, or the example.** No "in this guide", no "let's dive in".
10	2. **Take a position someone could disagree with.** If the paragraph could be inverted without changing meaning, it has no position. Sign your stance.
11	3. **Name names. Use numbers.** Real competitors, real customer names, real version numbers, real file paths, real benchmarks. Cut "lightweight"; write "54 KB".
12	4. **Verbs lead. Nouns follow.** Imperative is fine. Active voice. Cut nominalizations ("the implementation of" → "implementing").
13	5. **Vary sentence length on purpose.** Long, long, short. Smooth uniform rhythm is the deepest AI tell.
14	6. **Prose carries the load; structure supports it.** Bullets are for parallel options. Paragraphs are for argument. Don't bullet what would be tighter as a sentence.
15	7. **Plain words. Technical terms only when something specifically rests on them.** Mixing levels lets the technical terms hit harder.
16	8. **Allow ungrammatical fragments for rhythm.** Five words. Confidence signal.
17	9. **Respect the reader's competence.** No "developers should consider"; just "you might not need an effect".
18	10. **Read it aloud. Fix anything you stumble over.**
19	11. **Concrete over comprehensive.** Coverage is an AI obsession. Trade coverage for momentum. Leave things out.
20	12. **Close by handing off the next move.** Don't summarize. End on the strongest sentence, give a directive ("Now do this"), or just stop.
21	
22	## Denylist
23	
24	The build's `validateProse` step (in `scripts/build.js`) fails the build on these. The list is the editorial brief, enforced. Add a rule here when you ban a new pattern; remove a rule when the term has earned a real meaning here. **Do not silently allowlist** by working around the regex.
25	
26	### Stolen-engineer diction
27	Engineering words that became AI flavor once they leaked into training data around late 2024.
28	
29	| Banned | Why | Use instead |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| `load-bearing` | Almost always vague. The literal sense is rare. | Name the specific thing it does. "The decision that shapes the rest", "carries the brand", "matters specifically". |
32	| `highest-leverage` | Vague claim of impact. | Say what specifically pays off. "The change that moves the design most". |
33	| `biggest unlock` | Marketing-speak. | Describe the actual change. |
34	
35	### Internal jargon leaking out
36	Words that work in a research notebook and fail in user copy.
37	
38	| Banned | Why | Use instead |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| `reflex defaults` | Eval-team jargon. | "Instincts", "first guesses", "default reaches". |
41	| `collapses into monoculture` | Eval-paper voice. | Describe what specifically went wrong (e.g. "every model picked the same three fonts"). |
42	| `data-driven` | Empty marketing adjective. | Cite the data. "Validated against 15 briefs across two models". |
43	
44	### Marketing voice
45	Adjectives and verbs that gesture at quality without doing the work.
46	
47	| Banned | Why | Use instead |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| `seamless`, `seamlessly` | Hollow positive. | Say what specifically works without friction. |
50	| `robust`, `robustness` | Hollow positive. | Cite the failure mode handled. |
51	| `elevate`, `elevates` | Marketing verb. | Use the specific verb (improve, raise, sharpen). |
52	| `empower`, `empowers` | Marketing verb. | "Let you", "make possible". |
53	| `underscore`, `underscores` | AI tell. | "Show", "make clear". |
54	| `pivotal` | Hollow positive. | "Central", "key", or describe the role. |
55	| `tapestry` | AI scenery noun. | Cut. |
56	
57	### Verbs
58	| Banned | Why | Use instead |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| `delve`, `delves`, `delved`, `delving` | The most-flagged AI tell of all. | "Look at", "explore", or just delete the throat-clearing verb. |
61	
62	### Throat-clearing
63	Sentences that delay the point. Cut them; almost nothing of value is lost.
64	
65	| Banned | Why | Use instead |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| `in today's …` | Generic opener. | Start at the actual point. |
68	| `gone are the days` | Cliché opener. | Make the point directly. |
69	| `whether you're …` | Audience-pandering; addresses no one. | Pick one reader. Write to them. |
70	| `let's dive in` | Throat-clearing. | Just start. |
71	
72	### Closers
73	| Banned | Why | Use instead |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| `in summary`, `in conclusion` | Restates what was just said. | End on the strongest sentence. Trust the reader. |
76	
77	### Transitions
78	| Banned | Why | Use instead |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| `moreover`, `furthermore` | Metronome transition crutch. | Drop, or use "also", or restructure. |
81	
82	### Punctuation
83	| Banned | Why | Use instead |
84	|---|---|---|
85	| Em dash `—` (and HTML entities `&mdash;`, `&#8212;`, `&#x2014;`) | Decision-avoidance: writer didn't pick a relationship between the clauses. | Comma, colon, semicolon, period, parentheses. Pick the relationship. |
86	| ` -- ` (double hyphen as em-dash substitute) | Worse than the em dash. Signals failed cleanup. | Real punctuation. |
87	
88	## Patterns the validator can't catch
89	
90	The above are the easy wins. The deeper issues require human judgment on every paragraph.
91	
92	- **Negation pivot.** "It's not just X, it's Y." "Less about X, more about Y." This is now a stronger AI tell than any vocabulary item. Use sparingly. Most instances should be replaced with a direct positive claim.
93	- **Triadic everything.** Every list exactly three items. Every adjective in groups of three ("fast, simple, and powerful"). Vary count: use 2 or 4. Use 1.
94	- **The five-paragraph essay shape.** Intro → 3 sections → conclusion, on every page. Mix it up. Lead with the example. Skip the conclusion. Let some sections be one sentence.
95	- **Uniform paragraph length.** Insert a 4-word sentence. Insert a one-line paragraph.
96	- **Synthetic balance.** Pros and cons of equal length when one is clearly right. Write the recommendation; note real exceptions briefly.
97	- **Hollow confidence.** "Powerful" without numbers. Replace with a concrete fact.
98	- **Hedging stacks.** "It might potentially be useful to consider..." Each hedge is fine; stacked, they sound trained.
99	- **Interchangeable copy.** Swap "Impeccable" for a competitor name. If nothing becomes false, the copy is generic.
100	
101	## When in doubt
102	
103	Read the paragraph aloud. If you stumble, rewrite. If a sentence describes nothing specific to this product, cut it.
104
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# deadreckon HOWTO
2	
3	This repo builds a Rust CLI named `deadreckon` for unattended coding runs.
4	The CLI is the control plane; the TUI is an attachable live dashboard.
5	
6	DeadReckon is for people who already use agent CLIs and need unattended,
7	sandboxed, auditable work with a real definition of done. It is the harness around
8	those harnesses: provider CLIs do the coding while DeadReckon owns isolation,
9	done criteria, lifecycle, logs, evidence, recovery, and promotion. It supervises
10	agent CLIs instead of replacing them.
11	
12	For a first serious run:
13	
14	```bash
15	deadreckon start "build the app"
16	deadreckon attach latest
17	deadreckon status latest
18	deadreckon list
19	deadreckon finish latest
20	```
21	
22	## New User Path
23	
24	Use `start` when you want DeadReckon to choose the right first path and tell you
25	exactly what is missing:
26	
27	```bash
28	deadreckon start "build the app"
29	deadreckon attach latest
30	deadreckon status latest
31	deadreckon list
32	deadreckon finish latest
33	```
34	
35	In a TTY, `start` presents selection prompts for mode, provider, missing done
36	criteria, source mode, and final confirmation. For scripts, pass explicit flags
37	with `--yes`, `--plain`, `--quiet`, or `--json` so it never waits for input.
38	
39	If setup is incomplete, `start` stops before launching work and prints concrete
40	`try:` lines for setup, done criteria, or source mode. Paste the suggested
41	commands, then run the same `deadreckon start "build the app"` command again.
42	
43	If this repo already has completed deadreckon history, TTY `start` can offer a
44	follow-up from the latest extendable run, a new review pass, or a new full-plan
45	pass. For scripts, use preview first:
46	
47	```bash
48	deadreckon start "add settings" --preview --plain
49	deadreckon extend <run-id> "add settings"
50	deadreckon start "add settings" --mode review --yes
51	deadreckon start "add settings" --mode full-plan --yes
52	```
53	
54	When done criteria already exist, TTY `start` shows the current criteria and
55	offers keep, view, check, update, or cancel before launch. You can inspect or
56	change the same contract directly:
57	
58	```bash
59	deadreckon def-done show
60	deadreckon def-done check
61	deadreckon def-done "what should count as done"
62	```
63	
64	## Normal Single Run
65	
66	Use `run` directly when you already know this should be one supervised coding
67	run:
68	
69	```bash
70	deadreckon run "goal"
71	deadreckon attach latest
72	deadreckon finish latest
73	```
74	
75	`run` is still the canonical power-user command for source-mode flags, spend
76	caps, sandbox overrides, and one-run scripting.
77	
78	## Multi-Agent Work
79	
80	Use `orchestrate` directly when the goal needs a coder/reviewer pass or a
81	planner-led split into child runs:
82	
83	```bash
84	deadreckon orchestrate review "goal" --yes
85	deadreckon orchestrate full-plan "goal" --n 4 --yes
86	deadreckon attach latest
87	deadreckon finish latest
88	```
89	
90	`start --mode review` and `start --mode full-plan` route through the same
91	orchestration machinery when you want the guided front door first.
92	
93	## Build And Install Alias
94	
95	```bash
96	cd /Users/gdc/deadreckon
97	make build
98	make alias-zsh
99	source /Users/gdc/.zshrc
100	deadreckon --help
101	```
102	
103	The alias points to:
104	
105	```bash
106	/Users/gdc/deadreckon/target/release/deadreckon
107	```
108	
109	## Shell Tab Completion
110	
111	`deadreckon init` installs shell completion automatically when it can detect
112	your shell. To install or repair it later:
113	
114	```bash
115	deadreckon completion install
116	```
117	
118	That writes the generated script to the normal location for your shell. For zsh
119	it also adds a managed `.zshrc` block that loads `~/.zsh/completions`.
120	
121	Override detection or print a raw script:
122	
123	```bash
124	deadreckon completion install --shell zsh
125	deadreckon completion zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_deadreckon
126	```
127	
128	## Make Targets
129	
130	```bash
131	make help             # list targets
132	make build            # cargo build --release
133	make verify           # release build, tests, clippy, fmt check
134	make smoke            # keyless local smoke run
135	make doctor           # run deadreckon doctor
136	make stress           # 5 concurrent runs; defaults to 10 minutes
137	make clean-runtime    # remove repo-local smoke state
138	```
139	
140	Override runtime locations or stress duration:
141	
142	```bash
143	DEADRECKON_HOME=/tmp/deadreckon-home make smoke
144	STRESS_SECONDS=30 make stress
145	```
146	
147	## Runtime State
148	
149	By default, deadreckon writes runtime state to:
150	
151	```bash
152	/Users/gdc/.deadreckon
153	```
154	
155	For disposable tests, set:
156	
157	```bash
158	export DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.try-deadreckon
159	```
160	
161	Per-run artifacts include:
162	
163	```text
164	state.json
165	history.json
166	events.jsonl
167	traces.jsonl
168	spend.jsonl
169	provenance.jsonl
170	snapshots/turn-<N>/
171	proofs/turn-acceptance.json
172	working/ or library/<scope>/<run-id>/
173	```
174	
175	Completed accepted runs are promoted to:
176	
177	```bash
178	/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/library/<scope>/<run-id>/
179	```
180	
181	The directory where you launch `deadreckon run` is recorded as `launch-dir`.
182	In a git repo, the normal default is a separate worktree on a `dr/...` branch.
183	Your checkout is left unchanged until `deadreckon apply <run-id>`.
184	
185	## First Run
186	
187	Interactive setup:
188	
189	```bash
190	deadreckon init
191	deadreckon doctor
192	```
193	
194	Non-interactive examples:
195	
196	```bash
197	deadreckon init --provider cli:codex --sandbox auto --max-spend 10 --no-confirm
198	deadreckon init --provider anthropic --api-key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" --sandbox auto --max-spend 10 --no-confirm
199	deadreckon init --provider openai --api-key "$OPENAI_API_KEY" --sandbox auto --max-spend 10 --no-confirm
200	```
201	
202	Inspect or edit config:
203	
204	```bash
205	deadreckon config get defaults.provider
206	deadreckon config provider
207	deadreckon config provider cli:codex
208	deadreckon config model
209	deadreckon config model gpt-5.1-codex --provider cli:codex
210	deadreckon config set defaults.max_spend 15
211	deadreckon config set defaults.sandbox auto
212	deadreckon config set providers.anthropic.api_key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
213	```
214	
215	## Keyless Smoke Run
216	
217	Use this to prove the harness works without provider keys:
218	
219	```bash
220	export DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.try-deadreckon
221	rm -rf "$DEADRECKON_HOME"
222	
223	deadreckon run "tiny hello rust" --smoke --sandbox none --max-spend 1
224	deadreckon list
225	deadreckon status
226	```
227	
228	The default list is compact, project-scoped, and shows eight-character run IDs.
229	Commands accept unique prefixes, so `deadreckon show 861c51bf` works when that
230	prefix is unique. Most run-id arguments also accept `latest` or `last`, resolved
231	to the latest run for the current project. Use `--all` for global history and
232	`show` when you need full paths, IDs, traces, docs, and next actions.
233	
234	Inspect the latest run:
235	
236	```bash
237	deadreckon show latest
238	```
239	
240	Then attach to or finish it:
241	
242	```bash
243	deadreckon attach latest
244	```
245	
246	## Normal Single Run Details
247	
248	After `init`, the normal path in a git repo is:
249	
250	```bash
251	deadreckon run "make a full task productivity tracker in nodejs that allows me to manage my day"
252	deadreckon attach latest
253	deadreckon status
254	deadreckon finish latest
255	deadreckon apply latest --autostash --cleanup
256	```
257	
258	`run` prints the run id and attach command as soon as state is created:
259	
260	```text
261	started run <short-id> (<full-id>)
262	attach: deadreckon attach <short-id>
263	```
264	
265	Before it creates state or files, `run` prints a preview. In a clean git repo,
266	the preview shows `mode: worktree`, the `dr/...` branch, the base ref, and the
267	worktree path. Use `--yes` to skip the confirmation in scripts or `--preview`
268	to print the block and exit.
269	
270	Mode overrides:
271	
272	```bash
273	deadreckon run "goal" --fresh                         # old empty working dir
274	deadreckon run "goal" --from .                        # gitignore-aware copy
275	deadreckon run "goal" --worktree                      # force git worktree
276	deadreckon run "goal" --base main --branch-name dr/my-task # customize worktree branch
277	deadreckon run "goal" --allow-dirty                   # seed dirty files into worktree
278	deadreckon run "goal" --in-place --i-know-its-a-lot   # edit current dir directly
279	```
280	
281	Outside git, interactive `run` offers git init, copy mode, or cancel.
282	Non-interactive runs outside git need an explicit mode:
283	
284	```bash
285	deadreckon run "goal" --from . --yes
286	deadreckon run "goal" --fresh --yes
287	git init && deadreckon run "goal" --yes
288	```
289	
290	The default config from `deadreckon init` supplies the provider, sandbox, `$10` spend cap, and `3600` second wall-clock cap. Use flags only when overriding those defaults:
291	
292	```bash
293	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex
294	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex --model gpt-5.1-codex
295	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:claude-code
296	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:claude-code --model sonnet
297	deadreckon run "goal" --provider anthropic
298	deadreckon run "goal" --provider openai
299	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox sandbox-exec
300	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox none
301	deadreckon run "goal" --max-spend 5
302	deadreckon run "goal" --max-wall-seconds 1800
303	```
304	
305	`deadreckon run --preview "goal"` prints the provider and model before creating
306	state. `--model` is per-run; `deadreckon config model ...` makes the model
307	default for that provider. For CLI providers, `provider default` means
308	deadreckon delegates model choice to Codex or Claude Code unless you pass
309	`--model`.
310	
311	Run docs use their own provider route. By default deadreckon uses
312	`defaults.doc_provider`, then an installed subscription CLI (`cli:codex` before
313	`cli:claude-code`), then the run provider. Override it per run when needed:
314	
315	```bash
316	deadreckon run "goal" --doc-provider cli:codex
317	deadreckon config set defaults.doc_provider cli:codex
318	```
319	
320	Spend above `$50` requires confirmation:
321	
322	```bash
323	deadreckon run "large goal" --max-spend 75 --i-know-its-a-lot
324	```
325	
326	## TUI
327	
328	Open the dashboard:
329	
330	```bash
331	deadreckon attach <run-id>
332	```
333	
334	The TUI shows:
335	
336	```text
337	run id, status, phase, goal
338	working directory
339	per-turn timer
340	compact spend/context telemetry
341	wide center-left tool-call/provider activity stream
342	narrow center-right live files being generated
343	bottom supervised process/status panel
344	completed-run Markdown docs view
345	provider activity from live Codex session logs
346	```
347	
348	Keys:
349	
350	```text
351	Ctrl-D   detach without killing the run
352	q        quit
353	Esc      quit
354	Tab      move focus between panels
355	j/k      scroll focused panel
356	PgUp/PgDn scroll focused panel by a page
357	```
358	
359	After a run completes, the TUI footer adds lifecycle actions:
360	
361	```text
362	a        apply a completed worktree run
363	b        abandon/discard a completed worktree run
364	d        toggle formatted RUN-NARRATIVE.md docs in the main panel
365	m        export a completed copy/fresh artifact
366	e        extend a completed copy/fresh run with a follow-up goal
367	s        show run details
368	```
369	
370	The docs view uses a Markdown parser and ratatui styles for headings, bullets,
371	inline code, fenced code blocks, links, horizontal rules, and task lists. Press
372	`d` again to return to provider activity. Scroll it with the same `j/k`,
373	arrow-key, page-key, and mouse-wheel bindings.
374	
375	## Generated Docs
376	
377	Every run writes `.deadreckon/docs/_incremental.jsonl` at turn boundaries and
378	emits a `docs_checkpoint` event. Completion then runs the doc polish step unless
379	you passed `--no-docs`.
380	
381	```bash
382	deadreckon doc latest
383	deadreckon doc latest --kind as-built
384	deadreckon doc latest --kind decisions
385	deadreckon doc latest --polish --overwrite
386	deadreckon doc latest --polish --doc-provider cli:codex --max-spend 0.25
387	```
388	
389	`deadreckon doc latest --kind decisions` prints the implementation decision
390	ledger: design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, open questions, and
391	multi-alternative decision details. The live working copy for those sections is
392	`implementation-notes.html` in the run working directory.
393	
394	The polish preview lists the provider, why it was selected, the four narrator
395	subskills, token budget, max spend, and inputs hash. `--no-confirm` skips the
396	prompt for scripts. Results are recorded in `polish.json` with one status line
397	per subskill.
398	
399	The TUI does not start, kill, resume, or undo runs. Use CLI commands for those controls.
400	
401	## Completion Actions
402	
403	Completed `run` and `extend` commands show the same lifecycle actions in the CLI:
404	
405	```text
406	completed action [a apply, b abandon, d docs, s show, q quit]:
407	completed action [m export, e extend, d docs, s show, q quit]:
408	```
409	
410	Worktree runs use `a` to squash-apply changes to the current branch or `b` to
411	abandon the worktree and temporary branch. Copy/fresh runs use `m` to export the
412	library artifact into a normal directory, `e` to start a child run from the
413	completed artifact, `d` to read `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, or `s` to inspect state and lineage. Pass `--no-hints` to
414	`run` or `attach` when scripting.
415	
416	The CLI aliases use friendlier lifecycle names:
417	
418	```bash
419	deadreckon finish latest                            # choose apply or export from run mode
420	deadreckon def-done "builds and passes tests"           # write done criteria
421	deadreckon export latest --dest ./finished-project   # copy an artifact to a normal directory
422	deadreckon keep latest --autostash --cleanup         # alias for apply
423	deadreckon abandon latest                            # remove a temporary worktree/branch
424	deadreckon status                                    # latest state and next action
425	deadreckon watch latest                              # alias for attach
426	deadreckon stop latest                               # alias for kill
427	deadreckon continue latest                           # alias for resume
428	deadreckon inspect latest                            # alias for show
429	deadreckon docs latest                               # alias for doc
430	deadreckon prune --completed                         # alias for cleanup
431	```
432	
433	`extend` is still available for completed worktree runs from the CLI. It creates
434	a new `dr/...` branch from the parent run's branch, so the follow-up keeps the
435	parent changes without applying them to your checkout first:
436	
437	```bash
438	deadreckon extend <worktree-run-id> "continue with the next change"
439	```
440	
441	## List, Show, Kill, Resume
442	
443	```bash
444	deadreckon list
445	deadreckon list --all
446	deadreckon status
447	deadreckon show <run-id>
448	deadreckon show latest
449	deadreckon inspect latest
450	deadreckon finish latest
451	deadreckon finish latest --dest ./finished-project
452	deadreckon finish latest --autostash --cleanup
453	deadreckon apply <run-id>
454	deadreckon apply <run-id> --autostash
455	deadreckon apply <run-id> --cleanup --no-confirm
456	deadreckon apply <run-id> --git-strategy merge
457	deadreckon apply <run-id> --git-strategy cherry-pick --no-confirm
458	deadreckon keep <run-id> --autostash --cleanup
459	deadreckon abandon <run-id>
460	deadreckon abandon <run-id> --keep-branch
461	deadreckon cleanup --completed
462	deadreckon cleanup --stale --escalate
463	deadreckon cleanup --all-scopes --completed --no-confirm
464	deadreckon prune --completed
465	deadreckon kill <run-id>
466	deadreckon stop <run-id>
467	deadreckon kill <run-id> --escalate
468	deadreckon resume <run-id>
469	deadreckon continue <run-id>
470	deadreckon resume <run-id> --from-turn 2
471	deadreckon resume <run-id> --max-wall-seconds 3600
472	```
473	
474	`finish` is the easiest completion command. For a worktree run it routes to
475	`apply`; for a fresh/copy run it routes to `export`; for an in-place run it
476	prints review, docs, and undo guidance.
477	
478	Re-running `deadreckon apply <run-id>` after the changes are already on the
479	target branch is safe: deadreckon reports `already applied` instead of creating
480	or failing an empty commit. Add `--cleanup` to remove the temporary worktree and
481	branch in that already-applied state.
482	
483	`resume --from-turn N` truncates reconstructed history to turn `N` and continues with turn `N + 1`.
484	
485	## Undo
486	
487	Restore the previous turn snapshot:
488	
489	```bash
490	deadreckon undo --run <run-id>
491	```
492	
493	Restore a specific turn:
494	
495	```bash
496	deadreckon undo --run <run-id> --turn 1
497	```
498	
499	Undo restores the run working directory from `snapshots/turn-<N>/` and records
500	an undo trace. For in-place runs, undo restores the original source path because
501	the agent edited that directory directly.
502	
503	## Done Criteria
504	
505	If a run has no custom acceptance spec, `dr-gate` checks that the working directory exists and runs `cargo test` when `Cargo.toml` is present.
506	
507	The normal path is English first:
508	
509	```bash
510	deadreckon def-done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
511	deadreckon def-done add "users can save drawings"
512	deadreckon def-done check
513	deadreckon run "goal"
514	```
515	
516	`def-done` asks the configured provider to convert plain-English criteria into `.deadreckon/acceptance.yaml`. Short pack names are available without a provider when they fit:
517	
518	```bash
519	deadreckon def-done add build
520	deadreckon def-done add node
521	deadreckon def-done add static-site
522	deadreckon def-done add browser
523	deadreckon def-done add playwright
524	deadreckon def-done add vite
525	deadreckon def-done add nextjs
526	deadreckon def-done add python
527	```
528	
529	Runs and chains prompt before starting when no project acceptance file exists. Helper scripts generated by packs or drafts live under `.deadreckon/acceptance/` and are copied into the run workspace before `dr-gate` executes.
530	
531	The compiled YAML looks like this:
532	
533	```yaml
534	name: notes check
535	checks:
536	  - kind: file_exists
537	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
538	  - kind: content_match
539	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
540	    pattern: "dead reckoning"
541	  - kind: build_success
542	    cwd: "{working_dir}"
543	```
544	
545	Supported check kinds:
546	
547	```text
548	cargo_test
549	file_exists
550	content_match
551	build_success
552	shell
553	```
554	
555	`content_match` treats `pattern` as a regex when valid, with substring fallback for simple text. Shell, build, and cargo checks record duration plus clipped stdout/stderr so failures are readable.
556	
557	The acceptance marker is signed with a run-local nonce. A marker written by the agent is refused.
558	
559	## Import Existing Tool History
560	
561	Read-only imports:
562	
563	```bash
564	deadreckon import claude-code
565	deadreckon import codex
566	deadreckon import cursor
567	```
568	
569	Default source roots:
570	
571	```text
572	/Users/gdc/.claude/projects/
573	/Users/gdc/.codex/sessions/
574	/Users/gdc/.cursor/chats/
575	```
576	
577	Override source roots for testing:
578	
579	```bash
580	DEADRECKON_IMPORT_CLAUDE_ROOT=/tmp/claude deadreckon import claude-code
581	DEADRECKON_IMPORT_CODEX_ROOT=/tmp/codex deadreckon import codex
582	DEADRECKON_IMPORT_CURSOR_ROOT=/tmp/cursor deadreckon import cursor
583	```
584	
585	Imports create synthetic `imported-<hash>` runs with normalized traces and provenance.
586	
587	## Sandboxes
588	
589	Backends:
590	
591	```text
592	auto
593	sandbox-exec
594	bwrap
595	docker
596	none
597	```
598	
599	Examples:
600	
601	```bash
602	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox auto
603	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox sandbox-exec
604	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox docker
605	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox none
606	```
607	
608	Use `none` only for explicit local verification. `doctor` reports which sandbox binaries are available.
609	
610	## Doctor
611	
612	```bash
613	deadreckon doctor
614	```
615	
616	Checks include:
617	
618	```text
619	config present and parseable
620	provider credentials or CLI binaries
621	sandbox binaries and versions
622	disk space
623	runstate write permissions
624	OS/kernel sanity
625	Claude/Codex subscription CLI availability
626	```
627	
628	HTTP provider pings are conservative. Enable live ping behavior explicitly:
629	
630	```bash
631	DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING=1 deadreckon doctor
632	```
633	
634	## Stress And Verification
635	
636	Full normal verification:
637	
638	```bash
639	make verify
640	```
641	
642	Ten-minute 5-run stress:
643	
644	```bash
645	make stress
646	```
647	
648	Short stress while developing:
649	
650	```bash
651	STRESS_SECONDS=30 make stress
652	```
653	
654	The stress test asserts completed states, unique scopes, provenance identity, and no leftover lock files.
655	
656	## Configuration
657	
658	Runtime config lives at `~/.deadreckon/config.toml`. Set `DEADRECKON_HOME` to
659	relocate all runtime state (config, runstate, library) for isolated local runs
660	or tests.
661	
662	Switch providers, models, or defaults:
663	
664	```bash
665	deadreckon init --provider cli:codex --sandbox auto --max-spend 10
666	deadreckon init --provider anthropic --api-key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
667	deadreckon config provider cli:claude-code
668	deadreckon config model sonnet --provider cli:claude-code
669	deadreckon config set defaults.max_spend 15
670	```
671	
672	Override per run:
673	
674	```bash
675	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex --model gpt-5.1-codex
676	deadreckon run --preview "goal"     # show route and model, don't start
677	```
678	
679	### Sandbox Backends
680	
681	| Backend | What it is |
682	|---|---|
683	| `auto` | Picks the right native sandbox for your OS (default) |
684	| `sandbox-exec` | macOS native |
685	| `bwrap` | Linux native (bubblewrap) |
686	| `docker` | Opt-in container sandbox |
687	| `none` | Off (unsafe for real unattended work) |
688	
689	Check what your machine supports with `deadreckon doctor`. See
690	[Sandboxes](#sandboxes) above for run examples.
691	
692	## Full Command Reference
693	
694	The production model is a small set of verbs; every other command stays
695	findable through `deadreckon help-all`, `<command> --help`, and completion.
696	
697	Default production model:
698	
699	```text
700	start         begin supervised agent work
701	attach        open the live dashboard
702	status        latest run and next action for this project
703	list          find runs and plans
704	finish        choose apply or export from completed work
705	doctor        check config, providers, sandboxes, disk, runtime
706	init          create local config
707	def-done      compile English "done" criteria into checks
708	kill          stop a live run, chain, or plan
709	resume        continue an interrupted run
710	cleanup       clean abandoned, stale, or completed worktrees
711	help-all      show every advanced and compatibility command
712	```
713	
714	Power-user and advanced commands:
715	
716	```text
717	run           start one unattended coding run directly
718	orchestrate   one-command review / full-plan multi-agent runs
719	chain         plan and run ordered multi-step work
720	plan          write an orchestration plan (no child runs yet)
721	fork          start a plan's ready child runs
722	merge         compose plan children into one promoted artifact
723	apply         apply a completed worktree run to your branch
724	export        copy a completed artifact to a normal directory
725	extend        continue from a completed run
726	show          inspect state, lineage, spend, files
727	doc           print or export run documentation
728	rewind        preview or apply a provider flight checkpoint
729	history       search durable traces and provenance
730	library       query promoted run artifacts
731	providers     list provider routes (detect probes availability)
732	detect        probe registered providers
733	config        inspect or edit config keys
734	update        check for or apply self-updates
735	learn         index run evidence and propose improvements
736	improve       run evidence-gated self-improvement candidates
737	import        normalize histories from other coding tools
738	undo          restore a previous turn snapshot
739	abandon       remove a worktree run and temporary branch
740	completion    install shell tab-completion
741	```
742	
743	Aliases: `keep` → `apply`, `materialize` → `export`, `discard` → `abandon`,
744	`prune` → `cleanup`, `follow-up` → `extend`, `continue` → `resume`,
745	`stop` → `kill`, `next` → `status`.
746	
747	## Troubleshooting
748	
749	Run:
750	
751	```bash
752	deadreckon doctor
753	deadreckon list
754	deadreckon show <run-id>
755	```
756	
757	Common fixes:
758	
759	```bash
760	deadreckon init
761	deadreckon config set defaults.provider cli:codex
762	deadreckon config set defaults.sandbox auto
763	deadreckon kill <run-id> --escalate
764	deadreckon resume <run-id>
765	```
766	
767	If the alias does not exist in the current shell:
768	
769	```bash
770	source /Users/gdc/.zshrc
771	alias deadreckon
772	```
773
```

6	Built with Astro. Static output. One page so far; the page is the product

9	## Run it
10	
11	```bash
12	bun install
13	bun run dev      # local dev server on http://localhost:4321
14	bun run build    # static output to ./dist
15	```
16	
17	Use `pnpm` or `npm` if you prefer; the lockfile is bun's.
18	
19	## Editorial rules
20	
21	Copy follows the rules in `/Users/gdc/impeccable/STYLE.md` (no em dashes, no
22	"delve", no "seamless", no "let's dive in"). When you edit the page, read that
23	file first.
24	
25	Two cardinal rules specific to this site:
26	
27	1. **Don't oversell the watchdog.** The `dr-gate` signature is a hash plus
28	   filesystem isolation of the nonce, not crypto. Say so on the page and in
29	   the FAQ. The integrity story is real; the precise framing is what makes it
30	   trustworthy.
31	2. **Mention real commands, not hypothetical ones.** Every command in a code
32	   block should be one you can paste into a working deadreckon install.
33	
34	## Structure
35	
36	```
37	src/
38	  layouts/Base.astro    one shared layout (header + footer)
39	  components/

44	  styles/
45	    tokens.css          colors, type, spacing, motion
46	    main.css            page-section styles
47	public/

49	```
50	
51	## Brand
52	
53	- **Wordmark green** is the accent. Pulled from the deadreckon wordmark
54	  (`docs/assets/deadreckon-wordmark.png` in the deadreckon repo).
55	- **Bone paper** is the background. Warm, low-contrast, easy on long reads.
56	- **JetBrains Mono** carries headings. The product is a CLI; the type should
57	  say so.
58	- **Inter** is the body. Workhorse.
59	
60	If you change accent colors, change them in `tokens.css` (`--signal`,
61	`--signal-deep`, `--signal-ink`, `--signal-wash`) and audit the terminal
62	palette below; the green is shared between brand and terminal output.
