110	<span class="meta"># inside the run's sandbox</span>
111	<span class="prompt">agent$</span> <span class="you">cat /run/gate/nonce</span>
112	<span class="fail">cat: /run/gate/nonce: Permission denied</span>
113	
114	<span class="prompt">agent$</span> <span class="you">echo '&#123;"ok":true&#125;'</span> &gt; proofs/turn-acceptance.json
115	<span class="prompt">agent$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon finish latest</span>
116	<span class="fail">refused: marker signature missing</span>
117	<span class="fail">       expected: nonce-derived hash, got: empty</span>
118	
119	<span class="meta"># meanwhile, outside the sandbox</span>
120	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">dr-gate sign</span>
121	<span class="out">  read    </span>$RUN/gate/nonce <span class="ok">(0600, root-owned for this run)</span>
122	<span class="out">  hashed  </span>nonce + marker fields
123	<span class="out">  wrote   </span>proofs/turn-acceptance.json
124	<span class="ok">  signed ✓</span>
125	          </pre>
126	        </div>
127	
128	        <div class="quickstart-steps reveal">
129	          <div class="qs-step">
130	            <strong>01 · Isolated nonce</strong>
131	            <p>
132	              At run start, deadreckon writes a UUID nonce to <code>gate/nonce</code> outside the
133	              agent's sandbox root. The agent process has no read path to it.
134	            </p>
135	          </div>
136	          <div class="qs-step">
137	            <strong>02 · Out-of-band signature</strong>
138	            <p>
139	              <code>dr-gate</code> is a separate binary. It reads the nonce, hashes it with the
140	              acceptance fields, and writes the marker to <code>proofs/turn-acceptance.json</code>.
141	            </p>
142	          </div>
143	          <div class="qs-step">
144	            <strong>03 · Refusal by default</strong>
145	            <p>
146	              The main binary verifies the marker against the nonce before promotion. No valid
147	              signature, no promotion. The run loops, the agent gets another turn.
148	            </p>
149	          </div>
150	          <div class="qs-step">
151	            <strong>Honest scope</strong>
152	            <p>
153	              The signature is a hash, not an HMAC. The security property is process isolation
154	              under the default sandbox (<code>sandbox-exec</code> on macOS,
155	              <code>bwrap</code> on Linux), not cryptography. Turn the sandbox off, you lose the
156	              guarantee.
157	            </p>
158	          </div>
159	        </div>
160	      </div>
161	    </div>
162	  </section>
163	
164	  {/* ============================================ MENTAL MODEL ============================================ */}
165	  <section class="section" id="how">
166	    <div class="wrap">
167	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">How it works</span>
168	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">The agent owns the coding. <em>deadreckon owns the boundary.</em></h2>
169	
170	      {hasDiagramImage && (
171	        <figure class="diagram-figure reveal">
172	          <picture>
173	            <source srcset="/assets/diagram.webp" type="image/webp" />
174	            <img
175	              src={howItWorksImage}
176	              alt="deadreckon flow: your repo to isolated worktree to turn loop, with dr-gate signing the marker that promotes the run to a reviewable artifact"
177	              loading="lazy"
178	              decoding="async"
179	            />
180	          </picture>
181	        </figure>
182	      )}
183	
184	      {!hasDiagramImage && (
185	      <div class="diagram reveal" aria-label="Mental model: repo to worktree to signed gate to artifact">
186	{`  your repo (untouched)
187	        │
188	        │  def-done  "what 'finished' looks like, in English"
189	        │  deadreckon run   "what to build"
190	        ▼
191	  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
192	  │  isolated worktree on  dr/...  branch                       │
193	  │  ~/.deadreckon/worktrees/<scope>-<run-id>/                  │
194	  │                                                             │
195	  │   provider route ────►  cli:codex · cli:claude-code         │
196	  │                         anthropic · openai · smoke          │
197	  │                                                             │
198	  │   each turn: events.jsonl · spend.jsonl · traces.jsonl      │
199	  │              provenance.jsonl · snapshots/turn-N/           │
200	  └────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
201	                           │
202	                           │ checks fail?  agent gets another turn
203	                           │ checks pass?  ask the watchdog
204	                           ▼
205	  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐`}
206	<span class="gate">{`  │  dr-gate (separate process · holds the nonce)               │
207	  │      reads gate/nonce  ·  signs proofs/turn-acceptance      │`}</span>
208	{`  └────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
209	                           │ valid signature?
210	                           ▼
211	  promoted artifact
212	        RUN-NARRATIVE.md · RUN-DECISIONS.md · AS-BUILT-DELTA.md
213	        manifest.json · full provenance trail
214	        │
215	        │  deadreckon apply | export | extend | discard
216	        ▼
217	  your branch or library`}
218	      </div>
219	      )}
220	    </div>
221	  </section>
222	
223	  {/* ============================================ CAPABILITIES ============================================ */}
224	  <section class="section" id="capabilities">
225	    <div class="wrap">
226	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Capabilities</span>
227	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Five things you can do that the agent CLI alone can't.</h2>
228	
229	      <div class="cap reveal">
230	        <div class="cap-body">
231	          <span class="cap-num">01</span>
232	          <h3 class="cap-title">Your checkout is never touched.</h3>
233	          <p>
234	            In a git repo, <code>deadreckon run</code> opens a separate worktree on a
235	            <code>dr/...</code> branch under <code>~/.deadreckon/worktrees/</code>. The agent
236	            writes there. Your checkout sits exactly where you left it until you choose to merge:
237	          </p>
238	          <p>
239	            <code>deadreckon apply &lt;run-id&gt;</code>. Or <code>discard</code>. Or
240	            <code>export</code> the finished tree to a new directory and never touch your branch
241	            at all. Worktrees, snapshots, and the launch directory are recorded so resumes find
242	            their way back even after a crash.
243	          </p>
244	          <div class="cap-meta">Modes: <b>worktree (default)</b> · copy · fresh · in-place</div>
245	        </div>
246	        <div class="cap-visual">
247	          <div class="term">
248	            <div class="term-bar">
249	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
250	              <span class="term-title">filesystem after `deadreckon run`</span>
251	            </div>
252	            <pre class="term-body">
253	<span class="out">~/code/myapp/                </span><span class="ok">← your checkout, unchanged</span>
254	<span class="out">  src/...</span>
255	<span class="out">  .git/</span>
256	
257	<span class="out">~/.deadreckon/worktrees/</span>
258	<span class="out">  myapp-m7q3-build-a1f2/      </span><span class="accent">← agent works here</span>
259	<span class="out">    src/...                   </span>(branch: dr/build-the-app)
260	<span class="out">    state.json</span>
261	<span class="out">    events.jsonl</span>
262	<span class="out">    spend.jsonl</span>
263	<span class="out">    snapshots/turn-1/ ... turn-N/</span>
264	<span class="out">    proofs/turn-acceptance.json</span>
265	
266	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">git -C ~/code/myapp status</span>
267	<span class="ok">nothing to commit, working tree clean</span>
268	            </pre>
269	          </div>
270	        </div>
271	      </div>
272	
273	      <div class="cap cap--flip reveal">
274	        <div class="cap-body">
275	          <span class="cap-num">02</span>
276	          <h3 class="cap-title">Close the terminal. Open another. Attach.</h3>
277	          <p>
278	            The run lives on disk, not in your terminal session. Every turn writes
279	            <code>state.json</code>, <code>events.jsonl</code>, <code>traces.jsonl</code>,
280	            <code>spend.jsonl</code>, and a working-directory snapshot under
281	            <code>~/.deadreckon/</code>. The run keeps going whether you're watching or not.
282	          </p>
283	          <p>
284	            Type <code>deadreckon attach latest</code> and the TUI replays where the run is,
285	            what it edited, what it spent, and how many acceptance checks have passed.
286	            <code>Ctrl-D</code> detaches without killing. <code>deadreckon kill</code> stops it
287	            cleanly. <code>resume</code> picks up from the last completed turn.
288	          </p>
289	          <div class="cap-meta">Polling cadence: <b>events.jsonl every 500ms</b> · same-process bus when local</div>
290	        </div>
291	        <div class="cap-visual">
292	          <div class="term">
293	            <div class="term-bar">
294	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
295	              <span class="term-title">deadreckon attach latest</span>
296	            </div>
297	            <pre class="term-body">
298	<span class="out">┌─ run m7q3 · build the app ─────────────┐</span>
299	<span class="out">│ turn 14   wall 1h:42m   spend  $4.18   │</span>
300	<span class="out">│ provider  cli:codex     ctx 38% / 200k │</span>
301	<span class="out">├─ acceptance ───────────────────────────┤</span>
302	<span class="out">│ </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰</span><span class="out"> cargo_test      passed           │</span>
303	<span class="out">│ </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰</span><span class="out"> file_exists     passed           │</span>
304	<span class="out">│ </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰</span><span class="out"> content_match   passed           │</span>
305	<span class="out">│ </span><span class="warn">▰▰▰▱▱</span><span class="out"> build_success   running...       │</span>
306	<span class="out">├─ activity ─────────────────────────────┤</span>
307	<span class="out">│ 14:32  edit  src/auth/session.rs       │</span>
308	<span class="out">│ 14:33  edit  src/auth/mod.rs           │</span>
309	<span class="out">│ 14:33  run   cargo test --lib auth     │</span>
310	<span class="out">│ 14:35        </span><span class="accent">dr-gate signing marker...</span><span class="out"> │</span>
311	<span class="out">└────────────────────────────────────────┘</span>
312	<span class="meta">Ctrl-D detach · Ctrl-C never (use `deadreckon kill`)</span>
313	            </pre>
314	          </div>
315	        </div>
316	      </div>
317	
318	      <div class="cap reveal">
319	        <div class="cap-body">
320	          <span class="cap-num">03</span>
321	          <h3 class="cap-title">Undo turn 7. Keep turns 1 through 6.</h3>
322	          <p>
323	            Snapshots happen at turn boundaries, on disk, independent of git. So you can rewind
324	            a single bad turn without rolling back the whole run or rewriting branch history.
325	            The undo lands in <code>traces.jsonl</code>; the rest of the run keeps going.
326	          </p>
327	          <p>
328	            This is not <code>git reset</code> with extra steps. It works on the run's own snapshot
329	            trail, which means it works on <code>--in-place</code> runs in dirty repos and on
330	            non-git working directories too.
331	          </p>
332	        </div>
333	        <div class="cap-visual">
334	          <div class="term">
335	            <div class="term-bar">
336	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
337	              <span class="term-title">deadreckon undo --turn 7</span>
338	            </div>
339	            <pre class="term-body">
340	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon undo --run m7q3 --turn 7</span>
341	<span class="out">  restoring  </span>snapshots/turn-6/ <span class="ok">(working dir)</span>
342	<span class="out">  trace      </span>logged: undo-from=7 to=6
343	<span class="out">  state      </span>head turn now 6 · history preserved
344	<span class="ok">  done.</span> resume with: deadreckon resume m7q3
345	
346	<span class="meta"># turns 1-6 still in history, snapshots still on disk</span>
347	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">ls snapshots/</span>
348	<span class="out">turn-1  turn-2  turn-3  turn-4  turn-5  turn-6  turn-7</span>
349	            </pre>
350	          </div>
351	        </div>
352	      </div>
353	
354	      <div class="cap cap--flip reveal">
355	        <div class="cap-body">
356	          <span class="cap-num">04</span>
357	          <h3 class="cap-title">Get a reviewable artifact, not just a chat log.</h3>
358	          <p>
359	            deadreckon records which model call touched which files in
360	            <code>provenance.jsonl</code>. When the gate signs off, it writes a narrative,
361	            a decisions log, and a file-lineage manifest. You read the artifact. You don't
362	            scroll a transcript.
363	          </p>
364	          <p>
365	            <code>deadreckon doc &lt;run-id&gt; --kind delta</code> proposes architecture-doc
366	            updates when the run was broad enough to need them. That's how you keep
367	            <code>AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md</code> honest.
368	          </p>
369	          <div class="cap-meta">Outputs: <b>RUN-NARRATIVE</b> · RUN-DECISIONS · RUN-AS-BUILT · AS-BUILT-DELTA · manifest.json</div>
370	        </div>
371	        <div class="cap-visual">
372	          <div class="term">
373	            <div class="term-bar">
374	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
375	              <span class="term-title">RUN-NARRATIVE.md (excerpt)</span>
376	            </div>
377	            <pre class="term-body">
378	<span class="out">## What changed</span>
379	
380	<span class="out">Added password-based signup, login, and a saved-drawing</span>
381	<span class="out">route. New routes live in </span><span class="accent">src/auth/</span><span class="out"> and </span><span class="accent">src/drawings/</span><span class="out">.</span>
382	
383	<span class="out">## Why</span>
384	
385	<span class="out">The acceptance spec asked for three flows. Turn 4</span>
386	<span class="out">discovered an existing `User` model in `src/db/users.rs`</span>
387	<span class="out">and reused it instead of adding a parallel table.</span>
388	
389	<span class="out">## Files touched (provenance.jsonl summary)</span>
390	
391	<span class="out">  src/auth/session.rs       turns 3, 5, 7, 9</span>
392	<span class="out">  src/auth/mod.rs           turns 3, 9</span>
393	<span class="out">  src/drawings/save.rs      turns 11, 12</span>
394	<span class="out">  migrations/0004_auth.sql  turn 3</span>
395	<span class="out">  tests/auth_test.rs        turns 6, 8, 10</span>
396	            </pre>
397	          </div>
398	        </div>
399	      </div>
400	
401	      <div class="cap reveal">
402	        <div class="cap-body">
403	          <span class="cap-num">05</span>
404	          <h3 class="cap-title">Cap the spend. Cap the wall clock. Walk away.</h3>
405	          <p>
406	            Every provider response appends a record to <code>spend.jsonl</code> and updates the
407	            run total. Direct API routes (Anthropic, OpenAI) track dollar cost.
408	            Subscription CLI routes cap by wall-clock time, since the subscription already
409	            paid the bill.
410	          </p>
411	          <p>
412	            Pass <code>--max-spend 15</code> or <code>--max-wall-seconds 1800</code> and the run
413	            stops itself at the cap. Cross a high-spend threshold without the flag and you get
414	            an explicit confirmation, so a script doesn't accidentally launch a $200 run.
415	          </p>
416	        </div>
417	        <div class="cap-visual">
418	          <div class="term">
419	            <div class="term-bar">
420	              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
421	              <span class="term-title">deadreckon run --max-spend 15</span>
422	            </div>
423	            <pre class="term-body">
424	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-spend 15</span>
425	<span class="out">  spend cap     </span>$15.00
426	<span class="out">  wall cap      </span>none
427	<span class="out">  current spend </span>$0.00
428	<span class="out">  starting...</span>
429	
430	<span class="meta">...later...</span>
431	<span class="out">  turn 22 · spend $14.82 / $15.00</span>
432	<span class="warn">  cap reached after turn 22</span>
433	<span class="ok">  run paused cleanly · resume with: deadreckon resume latest</span>
434	            </pre>
435	          </div>
436	        </div>
437	      </div>
438	    </div>
439	  </section>
440	
441	  {/* ============================================ COMPARE ============================================ */}
442	  <section class="section" id="compare">
443	    <div class="wrap">
444	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Compared</span>
445	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">deadreckon doesn't replace your agent CLI. <em>It supervises it.</em></h2>
446	      <p class="section-lead reveal">
447	        Use the agent CLI you already trust for the coding. Use deadreckon for what the agent
448	        CLI was never designed to do: isolation, evidence, recovery, and a "done" you can
449	        defend.
450	      </p>
451	
452	      <table class="compare reveal" aria-label="Comparison with running the agent CLI directly">
453	        <thead>
454	          <tr>
455	            <th>Operational concern</th>
456	            <th>Agent CLI alone</th>
457	            <th>deadreckon supervising the CLI</th>
458	          </tr>
459	        </thead>
460	        <tbody>
461	          <tr>
462	            <td>Workspace safety</td>
463	            <td class="bare">Runs where you start it</td>
464	            <td class="dr">Isolated worktree by default. <b>Your checkout sits untouched until you say apply.</b></td>
465	          </tr>
466	          <tr>
467	            <td>Long-running attach</td>
468	            <td class="bare">Tied to the current terminal</td>
469	            <td class="dr">Run state is durable. <b>Attach from another terminal, or after a reboot.</b></td>
470	          </tr>
471	          <tr>
472	            <td>Spend control</td>
473	            <td class="bare">Visibility varies by provider</td>
474	            <td class="dr"><b>spend.jsonl per turn.</b> Hard caps on dollars or wall-clock.</td>
475	          </tr>
476	          <tr>
477	            <td>Undo</td>
478	            <td class="bare">Manual git, if it works</td>
479	            <td class="dr"><b>Snapshots every turn.</b> Restore turn 7 without losing 1–6.</td>
480	          </tr>
481	          <tr>
482	            <td>Provenance</td>
483	            <td class="bare">Transcript doesn't map cleanly to files</td>
484	            <td class="dr">Model/tool/file linkage written to <b>provenance.jsonl</b>.</td>
485	          </tr>
486	          <tr>
487	            <td>"Done" criteria</td>
488	            <td class="bare">The agent declares itself done</td>
489	            <td class="dr"><b>Out-of-process watchdog signs.</b> No marker, no promotion.</td>
490	          </tr>
491	          <tr>
492	            <td>Applying the work</td>
493	            <td class="bare">Tool-specific patch flow</td>
494	            <td class="dr"><b>apply · discard · export · extend</b> as first-class verbs.</td>
495	          </tr>
496	          <tr>
497	            <td>Multi-run coordination</td>
498	            <td class="bare">Left to the operator</td>
499	            <td class="dr">Scope/task locks prevent conflicting same-task runs.</td>
500	          </tr>
501	        </tbody>
502	      </table>
503	    </div>
504	  </section>
505

571	  {/* ============================================ TRY ============================================ */}
572	  <section class="section" id="try">
573	    <div class="wrap">
574	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Try without keys</span>
575	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">30 seconds. No API key. <em>Real loop, real gate, fake model.</em></h2>
576	      <p class="section-lead reveal">
577	        Smoke mode fakes the provider response. Every other moving part is real: the worktree,
578	        the sandbox, the snapshots, the spend ledger, the watchdog signing the marker. Verify
579	        the loop locally before pointing real money at it.
580	      </p>
581	
582	      <div class="term reveal">
583	        <div class="term-bar">
584	          <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
585	          <span class="term-title">smoke run · no keys required</span>
586	        </div>
587	        <pre class="term-body">

608	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Install</span>
609	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Install the RC. Prove the harness. Then choose your provider.</h2>
610	
611	      <div class="quickstart reveal">
612	        <div class="term">
613	          <div class="term-bar">
614	            <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
615	            <span class="term-title">install · configure · run</span>

620	
621	<span class="meta"># prove the harness without provider keys</span>
622	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon try</span>
623	
624	<span class="meta"># check local setup and available providers</span>

627	<span class="meta"># go</span>

629	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon attach latest</span>
630	<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon finish latest</span>
631	          </pre>

633	
634	        <div class="quickstart-steps">
635	          <div class="qs-step">
636	            <strong>Requirements</strong>
637	            <p>macOS or Linux, plus <code>curl</code> or <code>wget</code>. The RC installer downloads signed GitHub Release assets; no Rust toolchain is required.</p>
638	          </div>
639	          <div class="qs-step">
640	            <strong>Pin a version</strong>
641	            <p>The site installer defaults to <code>v0.1.0-rc.1</code>. Override by piping it into <code>DEADRECKON_TAG=v0.1.0-rc.1 sh</code>.</p>
642	          </div>
643	          <div class="qs-step">
644	            <strong>State on disk</strong>
645	            <p>Everything writes under <code>~/.deadreckon/</code>. Set <code>DEADRECKON_HOME</code> for sandbox-isolated tests.</p>
646	          </div>
647	          <div class="qs-step">
648	            <strong>Verify it works</strong>
649	            <p><code>deadreckon try</code> runs a keyless signed proof. <code>deadreckon doctor</code> checks config, providers, sandbox backends, disk, and runtime.</p>
650	          </div>
651	        </div>
652	      </div>

656	  {/* ============================================ NAME ============================================ */}
657	  <section class="section" id="name">
658	    <div class="wrap">
659	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">The name</span>
660	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Dead reckoning. <em>Navigation without perfect visibility.</em></h2>
661	      <p class="section-lead reveal">
662	        Sailors plotted dead reckoning when the stars were out of view. Track every move so you
663	        know where you are now. Long unattended agent runs face the same problem: partial context,
664	        a terminal that may be gone when you look back, a model that may have lied at turn 7.
665	        Don't trust the final answer. Navigate by evidence.
666	      </p>
667	      <p class="section-lead reveal">
668	        The questions deadreckon exists to answer:
669	      </p>
670	      <ul class="reveal" style="list-style:none; padding:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:var(--s-3); font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--fs-sm); color: var(--ink-soft);">
671	        <li>→ Where did the agent run, and what did it spend?</li>
672	        <li>→ Can I attach after closing the terminal?</li>
673	        <li>→ Can I undo turn 7 without rolling back the whole project?</li>
674	        <li>→ Can I prove the agent didn't mark its own work as accepted?</li>
675	      </ul>
676	    </div>
677	  </section>
678	
679	  {/* ============================================ FAQ ============================================ */}
680	  <section class="section" id="faq">
681	    <div class="wrap">
682	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">FAQ</span>
683	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Honest answers, including the ones that make this look smaller.</h2>
684	
685	      <div class="faq-list reveal">
686	        <div class="faq-item">
687	          <h3 class="faq-q">Does deadreckon replace Claude Code or Codex?</h3>
688	          <p class="faq-a">No. You still install the CLI you already use. deadreckon shells out to it, runs it inside an isolated worktree under a sandbox, and supervises the loop around it. The agent does the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.</p>
689	        </div>
690	
691	        <div class="faq-item">
692	          <h3 class="faq-q">Is the gate signature cryptographic?</h3>
693	          <p class="faq-a">No. The signature is a hash of the run nonce with the marker fields, written by a separate binary (<code>dr-gate</code>). The security property is filesystem isolation of <code>gate/nonce</code> under the default sandbox, not an HMAC or signing key. Run with <code>--sandbox none</code> and you lose the guarantee. The architecture docs spell out the scope.</p>
694	        </div>
695	
696	        <div class="faq-item">
697	          <h3 class="faq-q">What happens if the run crashes mid-turn?</h3>
698	          <p class="faq-a">The next <code>deadreckon resume</code> reads <code>events.jsonl</code> and <code>traces.jsonl</code>, ignores incomplete trailing entries, and restarts from the last completed turn. Snapshots are written at turn boundaries, so worst case you re-do one turn.</p>
699	        </div>
700	
701	        <div class="faq-item">
702	          <h3 class="faq-q">Can I run more than one at a time?</h3>
703	          <p class="faq-a">Yes. Each run scopes to a project; scope and task locks prevent two runs from clobbering the same workspace. <code>deadreckon list</code> shows everything in the current project, <code>--all</code> shows everything everywhere.</p>
704	        </div>
705	
706	        <div class="faq-item">
707	          <h3 class="faq-q">Does it work without a git repo?</h3>
708	          <p class="faq-a">Yes. Outside git, deadreckon falls back to copy mode (or <code>--in-place</code> if you insist). Worktrees are the default only when there's something to branch from.</p>
709	        </div>
710	
711	        <div class="faq-item">
712	          <h3 class="faq-q">What's still rough?</h3>
713	          <p class="faq-a">deadreckon is alpha. <code>deadreckon import</code> from other tools' histories lists what's there, but doesn't normalize it. Chains work but are deliberately tucked behind a separate subcommand. The Windows path isn't there yet; macOS and Linux are.</p>
714	        </div>
715	
716	        <div class="faq-item">
717	          <h3 class="faq-q">Where does state live?</h3>
718	          <p class="faq-a">Under <code>~/.deadreckon/</code> by default. Per-run: <code>state.json</code>, <code>events.jsonl</code>, <code>traces.jsonl</code>, <code>spend.jsonl</code>, <code>provenance.jsonl</code>, <code>snapshots/turn-N/</code>, <code>proofs/turn-acceptance.json</code>. Accepted runs are promoted to <code>~/.deadreckon/library/&lt;scope&gt;/&lt;run-id&gt;/</code>.</p>
719	        </div>

```text
1	# deadreckon: Concepts & How It Works
2	
3	The narrative companion to the [README](../README.md). If the README tells you
4	*what to type*, this explains *what deadreckon is doing and why you can trust
5	it*. For step-by-step usage, see [HOWTO](../HOWTO.md).
6	
7	## How it works
8	
9	1. **You write "done" in plain English.** deadreckon compiles it into executable checks: tests that must pass, files that must exist, scripts that must succeed.
10	2. **The agent runs in an isolated worktree**, inside a sandbox. Your real checkout is never touched.
11	3. **Every turn is saved** (state, spend, traces, file provenance, snapshots) so you can attach, kill, resume, undo, or audit any moment.
12	4. **A separate watchdog process (`dr-gate`) decides when the work is done.** It holds a secret the agent process cannot read, and signs the result with that secret. The agent cannot forge the signature, so it cannot mark its own work as accepted.
13	5. **If the checks fail, the loop keeps going.** The agent gets another turn. When the watchdog finally signs off for real, the run is atomically promoted to a reviewable artifact: narrative, decisions, file provenance, full audit trail.
14	
15	The loop is the product. The agent CLI does the coding. deadreckon decides when "done" actually means done.
16	
17	## Why this matters
18	
19	**The agent does the coding. deadreckon decides when it's done.**
20	
21	- **It can't fake the finish.** The watchdog (`dr-gate`) holds a secret the agent process can't read and signs the result with it. No valid signature, no "done." The agent literally cannot forge its own acceptance.
22	- **Walk away for real.** Every turn is saved to disk: state, spend, file lineage, a full snapshot. Close your laptop, lose the network, kill the model, then attach from another terminal and resume from the last completed turn. Nothing replays, nothing is lost.
23	- **You get evidence, not a transcript.** Each accepted run promotes to a reviewable artifact: what changed, why, which prompt touched which file, what it spent. Auditable on disk, not scrolled back in a chat window.
24	- **Bring the agent you already trust.** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, Pi, or a raw API key: deadreckon supervises any of them. It owns the boundary, not the intelligence.
25	
26	## Bring your own agent CLI
27	
28	deadreckon owns the run boundary; the CLI does the coding. Route any turn through the agent you already trust:
29	
30	| | Agent CLI (subscription) | Route |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| <img src="assets/providers/claude-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **Claude Code** | `cli:claude-code` |
33	| <img src="assets/providers/openai-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **Codex** | `cli:codex` |
34	| <img src="assets/providers/gemini-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **Gemini CLI** | `cli:gemini` |
35	| <img src="assets/providers/github-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | `cli:copilot` |
36	| <img src="assets/providers/opencode-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **OpenCode** | `cli:opencode` |
37	| <img src="assets/providers/pi-logo.svg" alt="" width="22"> | **Pi** | `cli:pi` |
38	
39	Prefer your own keys? Route directly to **Anthropic** (`anthropic`), **OpenAI** (`openai`), or any **OpenAI-compatible** endpoint (`openai-compatible`, e.g. OpenRouter, llama.cpp, local models). No keys at all? `--smoke` runs the whole harness against a faked provider.
40	
41	Already have history in another tool? `deadreckon import claude-code | codex | cursor` ingests it read-only as a run you can inspect.
42	
43	## The two things that make it different
44	
45	### Write "Done" In English, Verified By A Watchdog The Agent Can't Fool
46	
47	Tell deadreckon what success looks like in plain language. It compiles your sentence into executable checks that an independent watchdog runs:
48	
49	```bash
50	deadreckon def-done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
51	deadreckon def-done add "users can save drawings"
52	deadreckon def-done check
53	deadreckon run "finish the app"
54	```
55	
56	**Why the watchdog matters.** `dr-gate` holds a run-local secret the agent process cannot read, and stamps the result with it. Without a valid stamp, the run can't terminate, and the agent can't produce the stamp itself. If the checks fail, the run doesn't end; the agent gets another turn with a corrective hint.
57	
58	If no acceptance file is configured, the default is "the working directory exists and `cargo test` passes" (when `Cargo.toml` is present). Supported check kinds are `cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, and `shell`. Full reference, packs, and the compiled YAML format: [HOWTO § Done Criteria](../HOWTO.md#done-criteria).
59	
60	### Get An Auditable Artifact, Not A Transcript
61	
62	deadreckon records which model/tool call touched which files, then promotes each accepted run to a review packet:
63	
64	- `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` explains what happened.
65	- `RUN-DECISIONS.md` records the decision ledger: design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, open questions.
66	- `RUN-AS-BUILT.md` captures the subsystem shape after the run.
67	- `provenance.jsonl` links every changed file back to the turn, tool call, and model that produced it.
68	- `manifest.json` records what was built and from what.
69	
70	Agentic CLIs usually leave you with a patch and a transcript. deadreckon turns the session into a local published artifact you can inspect, export, extend, or apply. Doc kinds and the TUI docs view: [HOWTO § Generated Docs](../HOWTO.md#generated-docs).
71	
72	## What else it does
73	
74	Each of these is a first-class capability; usage lives in [HOWTO](../HOWTO.md):
75	
76	- **Your checkout is never touched.** Runs default to an isolated `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch; your real checkout changes only when you `deadreckon apply`. Copy, fresh, and explicit in-place modes are available too.
77	- **Crash-proof.** Every turn writes durable state. If the terminal dies, attach from another; if the run crashes, resume from the last completed turn.
78	- **Budgets and time limits.** `--max-spend 15` and `--max-wall-seconds 1800` cap a run, then walk away. High spend requires explicit confirmation.
79	- **Undo a single bad turn.** Snapshot-based rollback to any turn (`deadreckon undo --run <id> --turn 3`), recorded in the run trace, not just a `git reset`.
80	- **Resume, kill, extend, or export any run.** Runs are lifecycle objects, not one terminal session.
81	- **Autonomous chains for multi-step work.** Break a big goal into ordered steps, each with its own signed gate; the chain stops on the first gate failure.
82	
83	## The mental model
84	
85	```text
86	your repo
87	  |
88	  | deadreckon def-done "what 'finished' looks like, in English"
89	  | deadreckon run  "what to build"
90	  v
91	isolated worktree or copy   ◄── your real checkout untouched
92	  |
93	  | provider route: cli:codex, cli:claude-code, cli:gemini, anthropic, openai, ...
94	  v
95	sandboxed turn loop         ◄── agent works here
96	  |
97	  | every turn: trace, spend, provenance, snapshot, docs
98	  | check fails? agent gets another turn
99	  v
100	dr-gate watchdog            ◄── separate process, holds hidden nonce
101	  |                              agent CANNOT produce a valid marker
102	  | checks pass + signature valid?
103	  v
104	promoted artifact           ◄── narrative, decisions, file lineage
105	  |
106	  | inspect, doc, apply, discard, extend, export, cleanup
107	  v
108	your branch or library
109	```
110	
111	For multi-step work, `deadreckon chain` wraps this whole loop and runs N of them in order, stopping on the first gate failure. The agent owns the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.
112	
113	## Compared with agentic coding CLIs
114	
115	deadreckon doesn't replace Claude Code, Codex, or the rest; it supervises them. Use it when the task is too long, risky, or expensive to "run the agent in my checkout and hope I can reconstruct what happened."
116	
117	| Operational concern | Agentic CLI alone | deadreckon supervising the CLI |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| Workspace safety | Often runs where you start it | Isolated worktree by default; your checkout untouched |
120	| Long-running attach | Tied to the current terminal | Durable state; attach from another terminal later |
121	| Spend control | Varies by provider | Tracks totals; enforces spend and wall-clock caps |
122	| Undo | git-level or manual | Snapshots every turn; restores a specific turn |
123	| Done criteria | The agent may declare itself done | Requires a signed `dr-gate` marker before promotion |
124	| Output | A patch and a transcript | A promoted, auditable artifact with file provenance |
125	
126	Use the agentic CLI for intelligence. Use deadreckon for isolation, supervision, evidence, recovery, and promotion.
127	
128	## Why "deadreckon"?
129	
130	Dead reckoning is navigation without perfect visibility: track every move so you know where you are now. Unattended agents are the same problem: long task, partial context, the terminal may be gone when you look back. The name is the contract: don't trust the final answer, navigate by evidence.
131
```

```text
1	# deadreckon Production Design
2	
3	## Product
4	
5	`deadreckon` runs your coding agent unattended, and a separate watchdog process, not the agent, decides when the work is actually done. It is a Rust 2024 CLI harness that supervises agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi) and BYOK API routes rather than replacing them. The default user flow is `deadreckon run <goal>`: create durable run state, select a provider route, execute turns in a disposable sandbox, write spend/provenance/traces/snapshots after every turn, gate completion with a signature the agent process cannot forge, and make the run attachable, resumable, killable, inspectable, and undoable. The output is an auditable artifact, not a chat transcript.
6	
7	The production implementation is intentionally local-first. Runtime state defaults to `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`, and tests or explicit smoke runs can override that with `DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke` so this build process does not write outside the allowed implementation tree.
8	
9	## Reference Patterns
10	
11	- AS-BUILT §3: two-layer split. Rust owns state, locks, sandboxes, provider routing, and gates. Markdown skills under `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/` own agent-facing instructions.
12	- AS-BUILT §4: `state.json` per run, status enum, gap-numbered phase IDs, and `current/<task>.json` run pointers.
13	- AS-BUILT §6: JSON lock records with PID liveness and heartbeat stale reclaim.
14	- AS-BUILT §7-8: atomic promotion/gate markers are written by binary-owned verification, not by model prose.
15	- AS-BUILT §9: per-turn snapshots make bounded rollback possible.
16	- Claude Code mining:
17	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tools/BashTool/bashPermissions.ts` and `shouldUseSandbox.ts` inform command side-effect boundaries and sandbox warning posture.
18	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tools/shared/spawnMultiAgent.ts` informs inherited run context and multi-agent orchestration boundaries.
19	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/upstreamproxy/upstreamproxy.ts` informs fail-open provider/proxy setup and child-process environment merging.
20	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/ink/renderer.ts` informs ratatui attach rendering: bounded frames, no uncontrolled terminal state.
21	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/docs/prompts/` informs the Markdown skill shape in `skills/default-coding/SKILL.md`.
22	
23	## Workspace
24	
25	Source lives under `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`:
26	
27	- `crates/deadreckon-core`: run paths, phase machine, JSON state, codebase mode records, locks, heartbeats, snapshots, provenance, spend, traces, gates, imports, chains, and run docs primitives.
28	- `crates/deadreckon-runtime`: provider turn loop, sandboxed tool dispatch, cancellation checks, docs polish orchestration, `dr-gate` invocation, and promotion orchestration.
29	- `crates/deadreckon-providers`: BYOK config at `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`, provider trait, Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible, `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`, `cli:gemini`, `cli:copilot`, `cli:opencode`, `cli:pi`, and explicit `--smoke` scripted adapters, fallback routing, spend estimates.
30	- `crates/deadreckon-sandbox`: `sandbox-exec`, `bwrap`, `docker`, and `none` backends using `tokio::process::Command`; default `auto`.
31	- `crates/deadreckon`: clap parser, command handlers, ratatui attach UI, init/setup, config/settings, run, status/next, list/runs, doc/docs, attach/watch, kill/stop, resume/continue, undo/restore, show/inspect, import, materialize/export, finish/done, apply/keep, abandon/discard, cleanup/prune, extend/follow-up, library/artifacts, chain, and doctor/check.
32	- `skills/default-coding/SKILL.md`: Markdown skill loaded at runtime.
33	- `tests/`: workspace integration tests.
34	
35	## Top-10 Need Mapping
36	
37	1. Live Context & Spend Meter: `spend.jsonl` in `deadreckon-core`, spend summaries in `deadreckon attach`.
38	2. Multi-Agent Worktree Coordination: scope hashing, run pointers, and locks in `deadreckon-core`.
39	3. Infinite Undo For Agent Edits: per-turn `snapshots/turn-<N>/` plus `deadreckon undo`.
40	4. Prompt-To-Code Provenance Audit Trail: `provenance.jsonl` and `deadreckon show`.
41	5. Cross-Tool State Sharing: read-only import from `/Users/gdc/.claude/projects/`, `/Users/gdc/.codex/sessions/`, `/Users/gdc/.cursor/chats/`.
42	6. Agent Observability: `traces.jsonl` with LLM/tool/sandbox events and latencies.
43	7. Disposable Sandboxes: platform-native sandbox backends, Docker opt-in, `none` warning.
44	8. Billing Guardrails: `--max-spend <USD>` pauses runs when durable spend reaches cap.
45	9. Provider Routing / BYOK: adapters, CLI sub-agents, `deadreckon init`, `deadreckon config get/set`, and fallback chain configured from TOML.
46	10. Workspace Inventory & Run Queue: project-scoped `list`, `status`/`next`, `latest` run aliases, `attach`, `kill`, `resume`, `cleanup`, and state scan commands.
47	
48	## Execution Model
49	
50	The primary path is provider-driven: `deadreckon run <goal>` resolves the
51	codebase mode, previews the plan, creates state, and hands execution to
52	`deadreckon-runtime`. The runtime calls `ProviderRouter::complete`, parses model
53	actions, executes tool calls in the configured sandbox, feeds results into
54	history, writes docs, invokes `dr-gate`, and promotes successful runs. It
55	repeats until a provider returns `done`, a spend cap pauses the run, or the run
56	is killed. HTTP providers use user-supplied keys or env vars; CLI providers use
57	local subscription CLIs and run through the deadreckon sandbox wrapper.
58	
59	In a git repo, the default codebase mode is `worktree`: deadreckon creates
60	`~/.deadreckon/worktrees/<scope>-<run-id>` on a `dr/...` branch, runs the agent
61	there, and leaves the user's checkout untouched until `deadreckon apply`. Outside
62	git, interactive users can initialize git, copy the directory, or cancel.
63	Non-interactive users must pass `--fresh`, `--from`, or initialize git first.
64	The former empty working directory path remains available as `--fresh`.
65	
66	For keyless local verification only, `deadreckon run --smoke <goal>` selects the `smoke` provider explicitly. That scripted provider still goes through the same turn loop, sandbox dispatch, snapshots, spend records, traces, provenance, and external `dr-gate` acceptance marker; it is not the default run path.
67	
68	The default skill is Markdown and external to the binary. The binary loads it and records the skill name/path in state; it does not parse or mutate skill internals.
69	
70	## CLI Lifecycle
71	
72	Completed artifacts are promoted into `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/library/<scope>/<run-id>/`.
73	Worktree runs keep their `dr/...` branch available for review and finish with
74	`deadreckon finish <run-id>`, `deadreckon apply <run-id>`, or
75	`deadreckon abandon <run-id>`. `done` aliases `finish`, `keep` aliases `apply`,
76	and `discard` aliases `abandon`. `apply` supports squash, merge, and
77	cherry-pick strategies; `abandon` removes the worktree and, unless
78	`--keep-branch` is used, the temporary branch.
79	
80	Copy and fresh runs use `deadreckon materialize <run-id> --dest <path>` or the
81	`deadreckon export <run-id> --dest <path>` alias to copy the library artifact to
82	a user-owned path. `deadreckon finish <run-id> --dest <path>` routes to the same
83	export behavior for copy/fresh runs. These commands write
84	`.deadreckon/parent.json` and record the reverse `.materialized-to` marker in
85	the library. `deadreckon extend
86	<run-id> "follow-up goal"` preserves the parent's mode semantics: worktree
87	parents create a child `dr/...` branch off the parent branch, copy/fresh parents
88	seed a new working tree from the parent library, and in-place parents refuse with
89	a direct `run --in-place` hint. Extended runs store parent lineage in
90	`working/.deadreckon/parent.json` and start the normal turn loop with reset
91	resource caps.
92	
93	For normal operation, run ids accept unique prefixes and `latest` / `last`
94	resolve to the most recent run in the current project scope. `deadreckon list`
95	defaults to that current scope, `deadreckon list --all` shows global history, and
96	running `deadreckon` without a subcommand is equivalent to `deadreckon status`.
97	`deadreckon cleanup` / `deadreckon prune` remove abandoned, stale, or explicitly
98	selected completed worktree runs while leaving promoted library artifacts in
99	place.
100	
101	Lineage and codebase mode metadata intentionally stay outside `PipelineState`;
102	show/list/hints derive them from marker files and `working/.deadreckon/codebase.json`
103	so the state schema remains stable.
104	
105	Self-documenting run artifacts also live outside `PipelineState`. Each run
106	starts `working/.deadreckon/docs/`, appends deterministic per-turn records, and
107	attempts one `run-narrator` polish pass before promotion unless `--no-docs` is
108	set. Public copies land under `docs/` in the promoted artifact, and `apply`
109	builds its default commit body from the narrative and decisions docs.
110	
111	## Decisions And Conflicts
112	
113	- Runtime writes during verification: the rider prescribes `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`, while the build instruction forbids edits outside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/` and `/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/goals/`. The binary defaults to `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`, but all repository verification uses `DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke`.
114	- Sub-agent forking: orchestration records scope/session lineage and keeps the subprocess skill boundary; broader scheduling and richer coordination policy remain documented in `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
115	- Sandbox fallback: on macOS `auto` selects `sandbox-exec` if available. If not available, or on Linux without `bwrap`, `doctor` reports the missing binary and `run` falls back to `none` with a warning, matching the rider.
116	- Live Tier C CLI verification: `codex` was run with `exec --ephemeral --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` inside deadreckon's outer `sandbox-exec` wrapper. Run `59c57e4565704135a9982789d0754803` produced `working/notes.md`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, snapshots, and a validated `dr-gate` marker without raw API keys.
117	- First-run UX: `deadreckon init` writes `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`, `deadreckon config get/set` performs non-interactive edits, `doctor` prints actionable check/fix lines, and `run` enforces the `$50` confirmation guard for scripts.
118	- Codebase modes: the architecture keeps mode metadata in
119	  `working/.deadreckon/codebase.json` rather than extending `PipelineState`.
120	  This preserves existing runstate readers while allowing worktree, copy,
121	  in-place, and fresh flows to evolve independently.
122	- Crate boundary: `deadreckon-core` is adapter-free and owns durable schemas and
123	  primitives. `deadreckon-runtime` owns the dependencies on providers and
124	  sandboxes, so core tests and downstream readers can reason about state without
125	  pulling in HTTP, subprocess, or platform sandbox orchestration.
126	
127	## Verification
128	
129	Final verification target:
130	
131	```bash
132	cd /Users/gdc/deadreckon
133	cargo build --release
134	cargo test --workspace
135	cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
136	cargo fmt --check
137	DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke ./target/release/deadreckon run "tiny hello rust" --smoke --sandbox none --max-spend 1
138	DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke ./target/release/deadreckon init --provider cli:codex --max-spend 5 --sandbox sandbox-exec --no-confirm
139	DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke ./target/release/deadreckon config set providers.cli-codex.kind cli-codex
140	DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke ./target/release/deadreckon config set providers.cli-codex.binary codex
141	DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke ./target/release/deadreckon config set providers.cli-codex.extra_args '["--ephemeral", "--skip-git-repo-check", "--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox", "--ignore-rules"]'
142	DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke ./target/release/deadreckon run "make a 5-line file at notes.md describing dead reckoning" --provider cli-codex --sandbox sandbox-exec --max-spend 5
143	```
144	
145	`demo.cast` records real release-binary output from the live `cli:codex` path without relying on raw provider API keys.
146
```

1	#!/bin/sh
2	set -eu
3	
4	repo="${DEADRECKON_REPO:-gregce/deadreckon}"
5	tag="${DEADRECKON_TAG:-v0.1.0-rc.1}"
6	asset="${DEADRECKON_INSTALLER_ASSET:-deadreckon-installer.sh}"
7	base_url="https://github.com/${repo}/releases/download/${tag}"
8	tmp="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/deadreckon-install.$$"
9	
10	die() {
11	  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: $*" >&2
12	  exit 1
13	}
14	
15	download() {
16	  url="$1"
17	  out="$2"
18	  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
19	    curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$out"
20	  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
21	    wget -qO "$out" "$url"
22	  else
23	    die "install curl or wget, then rerun this installer"
24	  fi
25	}
26	
27	cleanup() {
28	  rm -rf "$tmp"
29	}
30	
31	trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM
32	
33	(umask 077 && mkdir "$tmp") || die "could not create temp dir: $tmp"
34	
35	printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: ${repo} ${tag}"
36	download "${base_url}/${asset}" "${tmp}/${asset}" || die "could not download ${base_url}/${asset}"
37	
38	if download "${base_url}/SHA256SUMS" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS"; then
39	  if grep "  ${asset}\$" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS" > "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS.${asset}"; then
40	    if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
41	      (cd "$tmp" && shasum -a 256 -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
42	        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
43	    elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
44	      (cd "$tmp" && sha256sum -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
45	        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
46	    else
47	      printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: shasum/sha256sum not found; skipping checksum verification" >&2
48	    fi
49	  else
50	    printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: ${asset} was not listed in SHA256SUMS" >&2
51	  fi
52	else
53	  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: could not download SHA256SUMS; skipping checksum verification" >&2
54	fi
55	
56	sh "${tmp}/${asset}" "$@"
57	
58	installed="${DEADRECKON_BIN:-${HOME}/.local/share/deadreckon/bin/deadreckon}"
59	if [ -x "$installed" ]; then
60	  bin="$installed"
61	elif command -v deadreckon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
62	  bin="deadreckon"
63	else
64	  bin="$installed"
65	fi
66	
67	printf '\n%s\n' "deadreckon install: next"

21	    wget -qO "$out" "$url"

24	  fi

34

36	download "${base_url}/${asset}" "${tmp}/${asset}" || die "could not download ${base_url}/${asset}"
37	
38	if download "${base_url}/SHA256SUMS" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS"; then
39	  if grep "  ${asset}\$" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS" > "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS.${asset}"; then
40	    if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
41	      (cd "$tmp" && shasum -a 256 -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \

48	    fi
49	  else
50	    printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: ${asset} was not listed in SHA256SUMS" >&2
51	  fi

54	fi

```text
1	# deadreckon-site
2	
3	Marketing site for [deadreckon](https://github.com/deadreckon/deadreckon), the
4	harness around the agent CLI you already use.
5	
6	Built with Astro. Static output. One page so far; the page is the product
7	brief, the docs live in the deadreckon repo.
8	
9	## Run it
10	
11	```bash
12	bun install
13	bun run dev      # local dev server on http://localhost:4321
14	bun run build    # static output to ./dist
15	```
16	
17	Use `pnpm` or `npm` if you prefer; the lockfile is bun's.
18	
19	## Editorial rules
20	
21	Copy follows the rules in `/Users/gdc/impeccable/STYLE.md` (no em dashes, no
22	"delve", no "seamless", no "let's dive in"). When you edit the page, read that
23	file first.
24	
25	Two cardinal rules specific to this site:
26	
27	1. **Don't oversell the watchdog.** The `dr-gate` signature is a hash plus
28	   filesystem isolation of the nonce, not crypto. Say so on the page and in
29	   the FAQ. The integrity story is real; the precise framing is what makes it
30	   trustworthy.
31	2. **Mention real commands, not hypothetical ones.** Every command in a code
32	   block should be one you can paste into a working deadreckon install.
33	
34	## Structure
35	
36	```
37	src/
38	  layouts/Base.astro    one shared layout (header + footer)
39	  components/
40	    Header.astro        sticky top nav
41	    Footer.astro
42	  pages/
43	    index.astro         the whole homepage
44	  styles/
45	    tokens.css          colors, type, spacing, motion
46	    main.css            page-section styles
47	public/
48	  assets/               wordmark, icon, logo (copied from deadreckon repo)
49	```
50	
51	## Brand
52	
53	- **Wordmark green** is the accent. Pulled from the deadreckon wordmark
54	  (`docs/assets/deadreckon-wordmark.png` in the deadreckon repo).
55	- **Bone paper** is the background. Warm, low-contrast, easy on long reads.
56	- **JetBrains Mono** carries headings. The product is a CLI; the type should
57	  say so.
58	- **Inter** is the body. Workhorse.
59	
60	If you change accent colors, change them in `tokens.css` (`--signal`,
61	`--signal-deep`, `--signal-ink`, `--signal-wash`) and audit the terminal
62	palette below; the green is shared between brand and terminal output.
63
```

```text
1	# Release Setup
2	
3	DeadReckon releases are built by GitHub Actions through `cargo-dist` plus the
4	release trust helpers under `release/trust/`. The agent may edit and test the
5	release pipeline, but creating tags, pushing tags, publishing packages, and
6	pushing the Homebrew tap remain operator actions.
7	
8	## Release Lanes
9	
10	| Lane | Trigger | Behavior |
11	| --- | --- | --- |
12	| Branch or PR | non-tag push or pull request | Runs `dist plan --output-format=json` and static release-policy checks only. No private secrets are required and nothing publishes. |
13	| RC | `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Builds release artifacts, requires official-repo macOS signing/notarization, generates `SHA256SUMS`, `release-manifest.json`, `release.spdx.json`, and GitHub attestations, then publishes a GitHub prerelease. It does not publish npm or Homebrew stable channels. |
14	| Stable | `vX.Y.Z` | Requires tag/version/changelog agreement, full verify, official-repo trust material, release artifacts, checksums, manifest, SBOM, GitHub attestations, npm provenance, and Homebrew integrity. |
15	
16	Stable Windows artifacts require Authenticode signing. If the Windows signing
17	secrets are absent, the stable release fails before any unsigned Windows artifact
18	can upload. RC and dry-run builds may still exercise the Windows target without
19	stable publication.
20	
21	## Official Artifact Contract
22	
23	Every official RC or stable release must produce:
24	
25	- cargo-dist archives and shell/PowerShell installers;
26	- the Homebrew formula artifact;
27	- npm wrapper and platform packages when the lane is stable;
28	- `SHA256SUMS`;
29	- `release-manifest.json`;
30	- `release.spdx.json`;
31	- GitHub artifact attestations;
32	- npm provenance for published npm packages;
33	- release notes or runbook commands that show verification steps.
34	
35	The workflow uploads the trust bundle explicitly after `cargo-dist` creates the
36	GitHub Release, then appends the checksum and attestation verification commands
37	to the release notes.
38	
39	Users should be able to verify a downloaded artifact with:
40	
41	```sh
42	shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
43	gh attestation verify <artifact> --repo gdc/deadreckon
44	```
45	
46	For macOS artifacts, CI extracts the cargo-dist archive, signs the packaged
47	`deadreckon` binary, verifies it with `codesign`, submits it with `notarytool`,
48	then repacks the archive that will be uploaded.
49	
50	## Required Apple Secrets
51	
52	Official RC and stable releases fail if any macOS signing secret is absent.
53	Forks, PRs, and branch dry-runs do not require these secrets.
54	
55	| Secret | Purpose |
56	| --- | --- |
57	| `APPLE_CERT_P12` | Base64-encoded Developer ID Application `.p12` certificate export. |
58	| `APPLE_CERT_PWD` | Password used when exporting the `.p12` certificate. |
59	| `APPLE_ID` | Apple Developer account email used by `notarytool`. |
60	| `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | Apple Developer Team ID. |
61	| `APPLE_APP_PWD` | App-specific password for the Apple ID used by `notarytool`. |
62	
63	## Required Windows Secrets
64	
65	Official stable releases fail if Windows signing material is absent.
66	
67	| Secret | Purpose |
68	| --- | --- |
69	| `WINDOWS_CERT_PFX` | Base64-encoded Authenticode code-signing `.pfx` export. |
70	| `WINDOWS_CERT_PWD` | Password for the `.pfx` export. |
71	
72	The Windows job decodes the `.pfx`, extracts the cargo-dist Windows zip, signs
73	`deadreckon.exe` with `signtool sign`, verifies it with `signtool verify`, then
74	repacks the zip and records Authenticode status in `release-manifest.json`.
75	
76	## Apple Developer ID Checklist
77	
78	1. Confirm the Apple account is enrolled in the Apple Developer Program.
79	2. In Keychain Access, create a certificate signing request for code signing.
80	3. In the Apple Developer portal, create a `Developer ID Application`
81	   certificate for macOS distribution.
82	4. Download and install the certificate into the login keychain.
83	5. Export the certificate and private key as a password-protected `.p12`.
84	6. Base64 encode the `.p12` without line wrapping.
85	
86	   ```sh
87	   base64 -i Certificates.p12 | tr -d '\n'
88	   ```
89	
90	7. Store the encoded value as the GitHub Actions secret `APPLE_CERT_P12`.
91	8. Store the `.p12` export password as `APPLE_CERT_PWD`.
92	9. Create an Apple app-specific password for the Apple ID used by CI.
93	10. Store the Apple ID email as `APPLE_ID`.
94	11. Store the Team ID as `APPLE_TEAM_ID`.
95	12. Store the app-specific password as `APPLE_APP_PWD`.
96	13. Confirm no `.p12`, `.pfx`, `.cer`, `.pem`, signing request, password, or Team ID
97	    material is committed to git.
98	14. Run a local smoke on a Mac before the first RC:
99	
100	    ```sh
101	    cargo build --release -p deadreckon
102	    codesign --sign "Developer ID Application" --options runtime --timestamp target/release/deadreckon
103	    codesign --verify --verbose target/release/deadreckon
104	    ditto -c -k --keepParent target/release/deadreckon /tmp/deadreckon.zip
105	    xcrun notarytool submit /tmp/deadreckon.zip \
106	      --apple-id "$APPLE_ID" \
107	      --team-id "$APPLE_TEAM_ID" \
108	      --password "$APPLE_APP_PWD" \
109	      --wait
110	    ```
111	
112	15. After CI hardening is merged, run an RC tag and confirm the workflow verifies
113	    the extracted packaged macOS archives, not only a loose local binary.
114	
115	## Package Manager Trust
116	
117	Homebrew stable publication requires `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`, a token with push
118	rights to `gdc/homebrew-tap`. The workflow verifies that the generated formula
119	checksum matches `SHA256SUMS` before committing the formula.
120	
121	npm stable publication prefers npm trusted publishing. Configure trusted
122	publishing in npm for `deadreckon` and each platform package, then set the
123	repository variable `NPM_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING=true`. If trusted publishing is not
124	available yet, set `NPM_TOKEN`; the workflow still publishes every package with
125	`npm publish --provenance`. Platform packages publish first and the wrapper
126	publishes last. The npm workflow validates the tag through the release trust
127	gate and refuses manual dispatches that are not official stable release tags.
128	
129	The release workflows require `id-token: write` for GitHub artifact
130	attestations and npm provenance.
131	
132	## Operator Release Flow
133	
134	1. Confirm the target tag is valid:
135	   - stable: `vX.Y.Z`;
136	   - RC: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`.
137	2. Confirm `Cargo.toml` workspace version and `npm/deadreckon/package.json`
138	   match the tag base version.
139	3. For stable releases, confirm `CHANGELOG.md` has a section for `X.Y.Z`.
140	4. Confirm Apple, Homebrew, and npm trust material are configured.
141	5. Confirm Windows Authenticode signing secrets are configured for stable tags.
142	6. Run focused local checks:
143	
144	   ```sh
145	   cargo test -p deadreckon --test release_plan
146	   cargo test -p deadreckon --test npm_wrapper
147	   cargo fmt --check
148	   git diff --check
149	   ```
150	
151	7. If `cargo-dist` is installed locally, also run:
152	
153	   ```sh
154	   dist plan --output-format=json
155	   ```
156	
157	8. Create and push an RC tag first. Review the GitHub Actions run, artifacts,
158	   `SHA256SUMS`, `release-manifest.json`, `release.spdx.json`, macOS signing
159	   evidence, and attestations.
160	9. After the RC rehearsal is clean, create and push the stable tag.
161	
162	The first real release remains an operator action.
163	
164	## Site Installer
165	
166	The website can host a thin bootstrap script at `https://deadreckon.sh/install.sh`.
167	That script downloads `deadreckon-installer.sh` from the GitHub Release selected
168	by `DEADRECKON_TAG` and then delegates to the cargo-dist installer. For the first
169	RC, the intended public command is:
170	
171	```sh
172	curl -fsSL https://deadreckon.sh/install.sh | sh
173	deadreckon try
174	deadreckon doctor
175	```
176	
177	Before announcing the command, confirm that the site script's default tag points
178	at the published RC and that the release has `deadreckon-installer.sh` plus
179	`SHA256SUMS` attached. For a pinned rehearsal:
180	
181	```sh
182	curl -fsSL https://deadreckon.sh/install.sh | DEADRECKON_TAG=v0.1.0-rc.1 sh
183	```
184
```
</details></tool-use>

163	        SL: Into<String>,
164	        SC: Into<String>,
165	    {
166	        let subject_kind = subject_kind.into();
167	        if subject_kind.trim().is_empty() {
168	            return Err(VerdictSurfaceError::MissingSubjectKind);
169	        }
170	        explanation.validate()?;
171	
172	        let primary = primary_actions
173	            .into_iter()
174	            .map(|(label, command)| HintLine {
175	                label: label.into(),
176	                command: command.into(),
177	            })
178	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
179	        if primary.len() != 1 {
180	            return Err(VerdictSurfaceError::ExpectedOnePrimaryAction {
181	                actual: primary.len(),
182	            });
183	        }
184	        let mut primary = primary;
185	        let primary_action = primary.remove(0);
186	        if primary_action.command.trim().is_empty() {
187	            return Err(VerdictSurfaceError::MissingPrimaryCommand);
188	        }
189	
190	        let primary_command = primary_action.command.clone();
191	        let secondary_actions = secondary_actions
192	            .into_iter()
193	            .map(|(label, command)| HintLine {
194	                label: label.into(),
195	                command: command.into(),
196	            })
197	            .filter(|action| action.command != primary_command)
198	            .collect();
199	
200	        Ok(Self {
201	            kind,
202	            subject_kind,
203	            subject: subject.map(str::to_string),
204	            explanation,
205	            primary_action,
206	            secondary_actions,
207	        })
208	    }
209	
210	    pub fn label(&self) -> String {
211	        match self.subject.as_deref() {
212	            Some(subject) if !subject.trim().is_empty() => {
213	                format!("{} {} {}", self.kind.as_str(), self.subject_kind, subject)
214	            }
215	            _ => format!("{} {}", self.kind.as_str(), self.subject_kind),
216	        }
217	    }
218	
219	    pub fn render_card(&self, options: &CardOptions) -> String {
220	        let mut sections = self.explanation.sections();
221	        if !self.secondary_actions.is_empty() {
222	            sections.push(Section::Blank);
223	            sections.push(Section::Lines {
224	                lines: vec!["Secondary".to_string()],
225	            });
226	        }
227	        render_card(
228	            &Card {
229	                title: TitleLine {
230	                    glyph: self.kind.glyph(),
231	                    label: self.label(),
232	                },
233	                subtitle: None,
234	                sections,
235	                primary_action: Some(self.primary_action.clone()),
236	                hints: self.secondary_actions.clone(),
237	            },
238	            options,
239	        )
240	    }
241	
242	    pub fn render_plain(&self, no_hints: bool) -> String {
243	        let mut out = String::new();
244	        out.push_str(&self.label());
245	        out.push_str("\n\nExplanation\n");
246	        out.push_str(self.explanation.what_happened.trim());
247	        out.push('\n');
248	        out.push_str(self.explanation.why_this_verdict.trim());
249	        out.push_str("\n\nEvidence\n");
250	        for (key, value) in &self.explanation.evidence {
251	            out.push_str(key);
252	            out.push_str(": ");
253	            out.push_str(value);
254	            out.push('\n');
255	        }
256	        out.push_str("\nRecommended\n");
257	        out.push_str(&self.primary_action.command);
258	        out.push('\n');
259	        if !no_hints && !self.secondary_actions.is_empty() {
260	            out.push_str("\nSecondary\n");
261	            for action in &self.secondary_actions {
262	                out.push_str(&action.command);
263	                out.push('\n');
264	            }
265	        }
266	        out
267	    }
268	
269	    pub fn verdict_json(&self) -> Value {
270	        json!({
271	            "kind": self.kind.as_str(),
272	            "label": self.label(),
273	            "subject": self.subject.as_deref().unwrap_or(self.subject_kind.as_str()),
274	            "recommended_command": self.primary_action.command,
275	            "explanation": self.explanation.one_line(),
276	            "evidence": self.explanation.evidence.iter().map(|(key, value)| {
277	                json!([key, value])
278	            }).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
279	        })
280	    }
281	
282	    pub fn add_to_json(&self, mut value: Value) -> Value {
283	        if !value.is_object() {
284	            value = Value::Object(Map::new());
285	        }
286	        if let Value::Object(object) = &mut value {
287	            object.insert(
288	                "primary_action".to_string(),
289	                Value::String(self.primary_action.command.clone()),
290	            );
291	            object.insert("verdict".to_string(), self.verdict_json());
292	        }
293	        value
294	    }
295	}
296	
297	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
298	pub enum VerdictSurfaceError {
299	    ExpectedOnePrimaryAction { actual: usize },
300	    MissingExplanation,
301	    MissingSubjectKind,
302	    MissingPrimaryCommand,
303	}

===== current README =====
<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/assets/deadreckon-wordmark.png" alt="deadreckon logo" width="640">
</p>

<p align="center"><strong>Run your coding agent unattended, and trust the result.</strong></p>

<p align="center">
DeadReckon is a harness around the agent CLI you already use.<br>
A separate watchdog process, not the agent, decides when the work is actually done.<br>
You get a signed, auditable artifact instead of a chat transcript you have to take on faith.
</p>

---

## Get started

```bash
cargo build --release          # binary at ./target/release/deadreckon
```

Then the whole tool is five commands:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `deadreckon start "build the app"` | Kick off a supervised run. Walk away. |
| `deadreckon attach latest` | Watch it work live. `Ctrl-D` leaves it running. |
| `deadreckon status` | What happened, and the one thing to do next. |
| `deadreckon list` | Find recent runs and plans. |
| `deadreckon finish latest` | Apply it to your branch, or export it. |

For a higher-level read while it runs, `deadreckon attach latest --view narrative` shows cited prose plus an evidence-backed visual map.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/assets/providers/claude-logo.png" alt="Claude Code" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
  <img src="docs/assets/providers/openai-logo.png" alt="Codex" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
  <img src="docs/assets/providers/gemini-logo.png" alt="Gemini CLI" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
  <img src="docs/assets/providers/github-logo.png" alt="GitHub Copilot CLI" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
  <img src="docs/assets/providers/opencode-logo.png" alt="OpenCode" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
  <img src="docs/assets/providers/pi-logo.svg" alt="Pi" height="34">
</p>

<p align="center"><sub>Supervises the agent CLI you already use: Claude Code · Codex · Gemini · Copilot · OpenCode · Pi · or any Anthropic / OpenAI-compatible API.</sub></p>

Everything else (budgets, undo, multi-step chains, provider routing) is optional power you reach for later. No API keys? `deadreckon run "hello" --smoke --sandbox none` exercises the whole harness against a faked provider.

> [!TIP]
> DeadReckon is on the production-release track. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, orchestration, and apply) is implemented and tested; release notes call out any compatibility migrations.

## Why it's different

- **It can't fake the finish.** A separate watchdog (`dr-gate`) holds a secret the agent process can't read and signs the result with it. No valid signature, no "done." The agent literally cannot mark its own work accepted.
- **Walk away for real.** Every turn is saved to disk. Close your laptop, lose the network, kill the model, then attach from another terminal and resume from the last completed turn.
- **Evidence, not a transcript.** Each accepted run promotes to a reviewable artifact: what changed, why, which prompt touched which file, what it spent.

→ The full story (the loop, the mental model, and how it compares) is in **[Concepts & How It Works](docs/CONCEPTS.md)**.

|---|---|
| **[Concepts & How It Works](docs/CONCEPTS.md)** | The loop, the watchdog, the mental model, supported agents, how it compares |
| **[HOWTO](HOWTO.md)** | Practical usage: setup, providers, sandboxes, configuration, every command |
| **[DESIGN](DESIGN.md)** | Product and architecture intent |
| **[As-Built Architecture](docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | Detailed implementation reference |
| **[Resume Semantics](docs/RESUME-SEMANTICS.md)** · **[Multi-Run](docs/MULTI-RUN.md)** | Crash/resume behavior and concurrency rules |
| **[V1 Candidates](docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md)** | Deferred features and roadmap |

DeadReckon is maintained as production-release software. The core lifecycle is implemented and tested, alongside multi-agent orchestration (`plan` / `fork` / `merge`), autonomous chains, the provider flight recorder with `rewind`, and a local self-improvement loop (`learn` / `improve`).

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

repo="${DEADRECKON_REPO:-gregce/deadreckon}"
tag="${DEADRECKON_TAG:-v0.1.0-rc.1}"
asset="${DEADRECKON_INSTALLER_ASSET:-deadreckon-installer.sh}"
base_url="https://github.com/${repo}/releases/download/${tag}"
tmp="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/deadreckon-install.$$"

die() {
  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

download() {
  url="$1"
  out="$2"
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$out"
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wget -qO "$out" "$url"
  else
    die "install curl or wget, then rerun this installer"
  fi
}

cleanup() {
  rm -rf "$tmp"
}

trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM

(umask 077 && mkdir "$tmp") || die "could not create temp dir: $tmp"

printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: ${repo} ${tag}"
download "${base_url}/${asset}" "${tmp}/${asset}" || die "could not download ${base_url}/${asset}"

if download "${base_url}/SHA256SUMS" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS"; then
  if grep "  ${asset}\$" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS" > "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS.${asset}"; then
    if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      (cd "$tmp" && shasum -a 256 -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
    elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      (cd "$tmp" && sha256sum -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
    else
      printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: shasum/sha256sum not found; skipping checksum verification" >&2
    fi
  else
    printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: ${asset} was not listed in SHA256SUMS" >&2
  fi
else
  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: could not download SHA256SUMS; skipping checksum verification" >&2
fi

sh "${tmp}/${asset}" "$@"

installed="${DEADRECKON_BIN:-${HOME}/.local/share/deadreckon/bin/deadreckon}"
if [ -x "$installed" ]; then
  bin="$installed"
```

# deadreckon

**Run your coding agent unattended — and trust the result.**

A separate watchdog process, not the agent, decides when the work is actually done. You get a signed, auditable artifact instead of a chat transcript you have to take on faith.

deadreckon is for builders, maintainers, founders, and engineering leads who already use agent CLIs and need those agents to run longer, safer, and more accountably than a raw terminal session allows.

Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, and the rest are good at writing code. They are not built to run for hours unattended and tell you, honestly, whether the work got done. deadreckon supervises them instead of replacing them.

## The whole tool, in four commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `deadreckon start "build the app"` | Kick off a supervised run. Walk away. |
| `deadreckon attach latest` | Watch it work live. `Ctrl-D` leaves it running. |
| `deadreckon status` | What happened, and the one thing to do next. |
| `deadreckon finish latest` | Apply it to your branch, or export it. |

That's the loop. Everything else — budgets, undo, multi-step chains, provider routing — is optional power you reach for later, all documented in [HOWTO.md](HOWTO.md).

> [!TIP]
> deadreckon is alpha software. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, and apply) is implemented and tested, but expect rough edges and breaking changes.

## Bring your own agent CLI


=== prior hero (parent of ea223a4) ===

# deadreckon

**A harness around the agent CLI you already use, so you can actually walk away.**

deadreckon is for builders, maintainers, founders, and engineering leads who already use agent CLIs and need those agents to run longer, safer, and more accountably than a raw terminal session allows.

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, and the rest are good at writing code. They are not built to run unattended for hours and tell you, honestly, whether the work got done. deadreckon supervises them instead of replacing them.

You bring the agent CLI you already trust. You tell deadreckon what "done" looks like in plain English. It runs the work in an isolated sandbox, saves every turn, and uses a separate watchdog process to decide when the run is actually finished: a watchdog the agent cannot fool.

```bash
deadreckon start "build the app"
# walk away, attach later from any terminal
deadreckon attach latest
deadreckon status
deadreckon list
```
